title: Feature: SQLite Storage Layer Core
description:
# SQLite Storage Layer Core

## Purpose
Implement the storage interface with classic bd semantics: transaction discipline, dirty tracking, blocked cache, and efficient list/search queries.

## Transaction Discipline (critical)
Every mutation runs in **BEGIN IMMEDIATE** transaction and must:
1. Apply change (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE)
2. Insert audit event
3. Mark dirty (issue_id and often depends_on_id)
4. Invalidate/rebuild blocked cache if status/dependency changed

## Required Operations
- Issue CRUD + reopen + delete/tombstone
- Dependency add/remove/list/tree/cycles
- Label add/remove/list/list-all
- Comments add/list
- Events add/list (DESC ordering)
- List/Search with filters (LIKE-based)
- Ready/Blocked queries (blocked cache)
- Dirty tracking + export hash ops
- Config/metadata get/set
- Child counters for hierarchical IDs

## Performance Patterns
- Batch label/comment/dep lookups for list/search outputs.
- Cache blocked set in `blocked_issues_cache`.
- Use indexes from schema bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Mutation steps atomic with proper event + dirty + cache invalidation.
- `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` used for writes; retry on SQLITE_BUSY.
- Query semantics match bd (ordering and filters).

## Tests
- Transaction atomicity: events + dirty marker on mutation.
- Ready/blocked cache invalidation on dependency/status changes.
- Batch query correctness.

title: Feature: Database Schema & Migrations
description:
# Database Schema & Migrations (SQLite)

## Purpose
Implement a schema **compatible with classic bd**. The Rust DB must match tables/columns/indexes/constraints so bd and br can operate on the same `.beads` directory.

## Core Tables (classic)
### issues
Fields (subset):
- Core: `id`, `content_hash`, `title`, `description`, `design`, `acceptance_criteria`, `notes`
- Workflow: `status`, `priority`, `issue_type`, `assignee`, `owner`, `estimated_minutes`
- Timestamps: `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`, `close_reason`, `closed_by_session`
- Scheduling: `due_at`, `defer_until`
- Tombstone: `deleted_at`, `deleted_by`, `delete_reason`, `original_type`
- Compaction: `compaction_level`, `compacted_at`, `compacted_at_commit`, `original_size`
- Messaging: `sender`, `ephemeral`
- Context: `pinned`, `is_template`
- Federation: `source_system`, `external_ref`

Constraints:
- Title length 1..500
- Priority 0..4
- Closed-at invariant (closed -> closed_at not null; non-closed -> closed_at null)

### dependencies
- PK `(issue_id, depends_on_id)`
- `depends_on_id` has **no FK** (allows `external:*` refs)
- `type`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `metadata`, `thread_id`

### labels, comments, events, config, metadata
- `labels` unique `(issue_id, label)`
- `comments` ordered by `created_at`
- `events` used for audit; not exported

### dirty_issues, export_hashes, blocked_issues_cache, child_counters
- `dirty_issues` tracks changes for incremental export
- `export_hashes` stores content hashes at export
- `blocked_issues_cache` materializes blocked IDs (+ blocked_by JSON per spec)
- `child_counters` tracks next child number per parent

## Indexes (must match bd)
- `issues.status`, `issues.priority`, `issues.issue_type`, `issues.assignee`, `issues.created_at`, `issues.updated_at`
- `dependencies.issue_id`, `dependencies.depends_on_id`, `dependencies.type`
- `labels.label`, `labels.issue_id`
- `events.issue_id`, `events.created_at`
- `dirty_issues.marked_at`
- `issues.external_ref` unique (non-null)

## Migration Strategy
- Legacy bd uses **idempotent migrations**, no `schema_migrations` table.
- For br: either
  - build a **consolidated schema** that already includes all classic fields, then
  - apply **minimal** idempotent migrations for forward compatibility.
- Do **not** include Gastown/HOP fields in schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PRAGMA table_info`/index lists match bd for classic fields.
- Constraints enforce title length, priority range, closed-at invariant.

## Tests
- Schema snapshot tests comparing to bd (`PRAGMA table_info` + indexes).
close_reason: Implemented schema. Forced close because dependency direction in tracker seems inverted (Schema is prereq for Storage).

title: export_hashes upsert silently lost under concurrent plain DB holder (exit 0) — update-time auto-flush path (GH #435)
description: GH #435 (NTM, 2026-08-20, verified on 0.3.2): with a second process holding a plain open connection to .beads/beads.db, br update's inline flush exports JSONL correctly and exits 0, but the export_hashes upsert is silently dropped — DB keeps the pre-change content hash, giving false 'in sync' answers to any consumer of the export ledger. Sync-time flush under a held read transaction was fixed by 0.3.2 (stalls ~30s then lands durably); the update-time auto-flush path still loses the upsert. On 0.3.0 both shapes were lossy incl. dirty_issues clear. Expected: bookkeeping lands durably (like the fixed sync-time path) or the command fails loudly/retries — never exit 0 with a stale ledger. Note: fsqlite bumped 0.3.1→0.3.6 on 2026-08-20; re-verify repro before fixing. Repro in the issue; reporter offers full transcripts.

title: Health sidecar detection must support custom DB filenames
description: Round-2 review found src/health.rs builds SQLite sidecar paths with Path::with_extension("db-wal") / db-shm / db-journal. That only matches beads.db-style filenames; SQLite appends sidecar suffixes to the full database filename, so a custom DB path such as issues.sqlite has sidecars issues.sqlite-wal and issues.sqlite-shm. Health classification can therefore miss truncated WAL and orphan SHM anomalies for custom DB paths. Use append-style sidecar paths and add regression coverage.
close_reason: Health classification now builds SQLite sidecar paths by appending -wal/-shm/-journal to the full DB filename, with custom filename coverage for orphan SHM and truncated WAL detection.

# stale Command (age-based filtering)

## Purpose
Report issues not updated in N days with optional status filters and clear JSON/text output.

```
br stale [--days N] [--status ...]
```

- Text: header `Stale issues (N not updated in D+ days):` with numbered list,
  including status, days stale, and assignee when present.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Correct default of 30 days and status filters.
- Accurate days-stale calculation from `updated_at`.
- JSON shape matches bd.

## Tests
- Issues with varying updated_at; verify threshold and ordering.

title: Implement user configuration system (.brrc / config.toml)
description:
# User Configuration System

## Purpose
Allow users to customize br's behavior through configuration files, environment variables, and command-line flags with a clear precedence order.

## Why This Matters
- Users have different preferences (colors, defaults, paths)
- Teams may want consistent configuration
- AI agents may need specific output formatting
- Power users expect configurability

## Configuration Precedence (highest to lowest)
1. Command-line flags (always win)
2. Environment variables (`BR_*`)
3. Project config (`.beads/config.toml`)
4. User config (`~/.config/br/config.toml` or `~/.brrc`)
5. System defaults

## Configurable Options

### Display Options
```toml
[display]
color = "auto"  # auto | always | never
format = "human"  # human | json | compact
pager = true  # Use pager for long output
unicode = true  # Use unicode symbols (✓, ○, etc.)
relative_dates = true  # "2 hours ago" vs "2026-01-16T10:30:00Z"
```

### Default Values
```toml
[defaults]
priority = 2  # Default priority for new issues (0-4)
type = "task"  # Default type for new issues
status = "open"  # Default status for new issues
```

### Paths
```toml
[paths]
database = ".beads/beads.db"  # Relative to project root
jsonl = ".beads/issues.jsonl"  # Sync file location
```

### Behavior
```toml
[behavior]
auto_sync = false  # Auto-sync after mutations
confirm_destructive = true  # Confirm before delete/close
check_updates = "weekly"  # never | daily | weekly | always
```

### Agent Mode
```toml
[agent]
structured_errors = true  # Always use structured JSON errors
verbose_hints = true  # Include detailed hints in errors
```

## Environment Variables
```bash
BR_COLOR=never
BR_FORMAT=json
BR_DATABASE=/custom/path/beads.db
BR_DEFAULT_PRIORITY=1
BR_NO_PAGER=1
```

## Implementation

### Config Loading
```rust
use figment::{Figment, providers::{Toml, Env, Serialized}};

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct Config {
    pub display: DisplayConfig,
    pub defaults: DefaultsConfig,
    pub paths: PathsConfig,
    pub behavior: BehaviorConfig,
    pub agent: AgentConfig,
}

impl Config {
    pub fn load() -> Result<Self> {
        Figment::new()
            .merge(Serialized::defaults(Config::default()))
            .merge(Toml::file("~/.config/br/config.toml").nested())
            .merge(Toml::file(".beads/config.toml").nested())
            .merge(Env::prefixed("BR_").split("_"))
            .extract()
    }
}
```

### Config Command
```bash
br config              # Show current config (merged)
br config --list       # List all options
br config --get key    # Get specific value
br config --set key=value  # Set in user config
br config --edit       # Open config in $EDITOR
br config --path       # Show config file path
```

## Files to Create
- `src/config/mod.rs` - Config loading and types
- `src/config/defaults.rs` - Default values
- `src/cli/commands/config.rs` - Config command

## Cargo.toml Additions
```toml
[dependencies]
figment = { version = "0.10", features = ["toml", "env"] }
directories = "5.0"  # For XDG paths
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Config loads from all sources with correct precedence
- [ ] `br config` displays merged configuration
- [ ] `br config --set` modifies user config file
- [ ] Environment variables override config file
- [ ] Command-line flags override everything
- [ ] Missing config file is not an error
- [ ] Invalid config produces helpful error message

## Testing Requirements

### Unit Tests
```rust
#[test]
fn test_config_precedence() {
    // Set env var
    std::env::set_var("BR_DEFAULT_PRIORITY", "1");
    
    // Write project config with priority=3
    write_config(".beads/config.toml", "[defaults]\npriority = 3");
    
    let config = Config::load().unwrap();
    // Env should win
    assert_eq\!(config.defaults.priority, 1);
}

#[test]
fn test_config_defaults() {
    let config = Config::default();
    assert_eq\!(config.defaults.priority, 2);
    assert_eq\!(config.display.color, ColorChoice::Auto);
}
```

### E2E Tests
```rust
#[test]
fn test_config_affects_output() {
    // Set no-color via env
    let output = Command::new("br")
        .env("BR_COLOR", "never")
        .args(["list"])
        .output()
        .unwrap();
    
    // Should have no ANSI escape codes
    assert\!(\!String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).contains("\x1b["));
}
```

## Logging
- Log which config files were loaded
- Log config merge order
- Log any config parsing warnings
close_reason: Implemented br config command with full subcommand support: show merged config, --list options, --get/--set values, --edit to open editor, --path to show config paths, --project/--user for layer-specific views. Supports JSON output. Tests passing. Display options (color, format, pager, unicode, relative_dates) deferred as separate enhancement.

title: Feature: Error Handling Module (error/)
description:
# Error Handling Module

## Purpose
Provide structured errors while matching bd's **legacy JSON error behavior** (stdout vs stderr quirks) and exit code conventions.

## Error Types
- NotFound / InvalidID / AmbiguousID
- Validation (priority/status/type/title)
- CycleDetected
- Conflict (import collisions, prefix mismatch)
- Database/IO/JSON errors

## Exit Codes (classic)
- Legacy bd typically exits **1** for fatal errors (even though docs list other codes).
- Some commands still emit plain text errors even with `--json`.

## JSON Error Quirks (must mirror bd)
- `FatalErrorRespectJSON(...)` emits `{ "error": "..." }` to **stdout** and exits 1.
- `outputJSONError(...)` emits `{ "error": "...", "code": "..."? }` to **stderr**.
- Some code paths bypass JSON helpers and print text to stderr.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Error messages consistent and helpful (include hint where possible).
- JSON error channel matches legacy behavior per command (see output schema bead).

## Tests
- Golden tests for JSON error output (stdout vs stderr) in key commands.
close_reason: Implemented complete error module with BeadsError enum, context extensions, and model types with all clippy warnings fixed

title: doctor: fail closed on non-regular .write.lock nodes
description: Doctor currently reports symlinked and other non-regular .beads/.write.lock nodes as OK while claiming a sibling TOCTOU detector will handle them, but no such detector exists and startup OpenOptions follows a symlink. Add an lstat-based fail-closed classification before open, stable robot/human diagnostics, no target traversal or inode replacement, and real fixture/E2E coverage for symlink and directory shapes.
close_reason: Landed in 2f32dcfc. Note: startup already refuses non-regular lock nodes via blocking_write_lock ('Refusing unsafe workspace write lock path', shipped with the 2026-07-27 sync-safety merge) — this bead's residual gap was doctor itself, which reported symlink/dir nodes Ok deferring to a nonexistent TOCTOU sibling. Doctor's write_lock check now fails closed (Error, reason=non_regular_lock_node, node_kind symlink/directory/fifo/socket/device) from lstat only, never traversing or replacing the node; permissions.write_lock explains its deferral. Proof: unit tests 6/6 (symlink+directory shapes), new fixture write_lock_symlink_node PASS (asserts startup refusal + node untouched through repair/undo), e2e e2e_doctor_write_lock_shapes 2/2 (directory shape fails doctor and mutating commands loudly, node untouched), clippy -D warnings green.

title: [MEDIUM] Dual OutputContext types: format::OutputContext is shadowed dead code
description:
Multiple dead/superseded public types in src/format/ have been replaced by src/output/ equivalents:

1. format::context::OutputContext (4 modes) → superseded by output::context::OutputContext (5 modes, adds Toon)
   - format::OutputContext only consumed by format::syntax and format::markdown (themselves never called from CLI/output code)
   
2. format::rich::RichIssueTable/RichIssuePanel/RichDependencyTree → superseded by output::components::IssueTable/IssuePanel/DependencyTree
   - format::rich types are never used outside src/format/rich.rs
   - format::rich also exports format_status_badge, format_count_badges, build_completion_bar — all dead

3. format::syntax::highlight_code and format::markdown::render_markdown accept format::OutputContext, not output::OutputContext — library consumers cannot call them with the active OutputContext type

Impact:
- Confusing dual API surface for library consumers

title: Feature: CLI Skeleton with Clap Derive
description:
# CLI Skeleton (clap derive)

## Purpose
Define the CLI surface and global flags to match classic bd semantics (non-invasive). This bead sets the **command list**, **global flags**, and output mode expectations.

## Global Flags (classic)
- `--db <path>`: DB path (auto-discover .beads/*.db if not set)
- `--actor <name>`: actor for audit trail
- `--json`: JSON output
- `--no-daemon`: force direct mode (daemon excluded in br)
- `--no-auto-flush`: skip auto JSONL export
- `--no-auto-import`: skip auto import (error if stale)
- `--allow-stale`: bypass freshness check with warning
- `--lock-timeout <ms|duration>`: SQLite busy timeout
- `--no-db`: JSONL-only mode
- `--verbose/-v`, `--quiet/-q`

## Command Set (classic v1)
Required:
- `init`, `create`, `update`, `close`, `reopen`, `delete`
- `list`, `show`, `ready`, `blocked`, `search`
- `dep`, `label`, `comments`
- `stats`/`status`, `count`, `stale`, `orphans`
- `defer`, `undefer`
- `sync --flush-only`, `sync --import-only`
- `config`
Optional (post-core): `where`, `info`, `version`, `q`, `lint`, `graph`, `epic`.

## Output Modes
- Text (default), JSON (`--json`).
- `--json` output must be stable; errors are **inconsistent** in legacy:
  - Some fatal errors emit `{ "error": "..." }` to **stdout**.
  - Others emit JSON error to **stderr**.
  - Some paths still emit plain text even in JSON mode.
We must document + test these legacy quirks for parity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Help output shows correct commands + global flags.
- JSON mode routing is consistent with bd’s legacy behavior.

title: JSONL Import Implementation
description:
# JSONL Import Implementation

## Purpose
Implement classic JSONL import semantics with collision detection, prefix validation, tombstone protection, and depth-ordered creation.

## Pipeline (classic)
1. **Conflict marker scan** (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) → abort.
2. Parse JSONL with 2MB buffer.
3. Normalize:
   - Recompute content_hash (ignore JSONL value)
   - If ID contains `-wisp-`, set `ephemeral=true`
   - Apply defaults (`SetDefaults`) + closed_at invariant repair
4. **Clear export_hashes** before import.
5. Prefix validation (skip in multi-repo or `SkipPrefixValidation=true`).
6. Collision detection (4-phase): external_ref → content_hash → ID → new.
7. Tombstone protection: if DB has tombstone for ID, **skip** incoming.
8. Orphan handling: `strict|resurrect|skip|allow`.
9. Create issues depth-by-depth (parents first).
10. Sync deps/labels/comments after issues.
11. Refresh blocked cache.
12. Update metadata (`jsonl_content_hash`, `last_import_time`).

## Prefix Mismatch
- If mismatches are only tombstones, drop silently.
- `--rename-on-import` rewrites IDs **and** text references in title/desc/design/acceptance/notes/comments/deps.
- Otherwise error.

## External Ref Duplicates
- Default: error on duplicate external_ref.
- `--clear-duplicate-external-refs`: keep first, clear others.

## Output
- Legacy import does **not** emit structured JSON summary; output is stderr text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Collision handling matches bd (timestamp-gated updates; equal timestamps skip).
- Tombstones never resurrect.
- Export hashes cleared before import.

## Tests
- Prefix mismatch + rename-on-import.
- Tombstone protection.
- Orphan handling modes.
- Collision detection order.
notes: JSONL import fully implemented in src/sync/mod.rs: import_from_jsonl() implements complete pipeline - conflict marker scanning, 2MB buffered JSONL parsing, normalization, prefix validation, 4-phase collision detection, tombstone protection, external ref duplicate handling, issue upsert, relation sync (deps/labels/comments), blocked cache rebuild, metadata update. All storage methods implemented in sqlite.rs. Tests pass.
close_reason: JSONL import fully verified - all 3 acceptance criteria met: timestamp-gated updates with equal timestamp skip, tombstone protection never resurrects, export hashes cleared before import. All tests pass (399 lib + integration).

title: Neutralize terminal control sequences in rendered issue fields
description:
Lens: Adversary

Finding: User-controlled issue fields can contain terminal control sequences. Titles, descriptions, comments, authors, and some event text are accepted with length-only validation and are rendered by multiple human-output paths. A malicious local contributor could craft issue data that clears the terminal, rewrites previous lines, spoofs output, or triggers terminal-specific OSC behavior when another operator runs `br list`, `br show`, `br audit`, or related commands.

Evidence:
- `src/validation/mod.rs` validates title/comment emptiness and length but not C0/C1/ANSI/OSC control characters.
- Several CLI and formatter paths print issue titles/comments/event text directly for human output.
- JSON output should remain raw, but human terminal output needs defensive rendering.

Acceptance criteria:
- Human output visibly escapes or strips dangerous terminal controls in all user-controlled text fields.
- JSON/robot output preserves raw values for machine consumers.
- Regression tests cover ANSI clear-screen, carriage return/backspace spoofing, and OSC-style sequences in titles/comments.
close_reason: Escaped terminal control characters in human output while preserving raw JSON; added sanitizer unit tests and E2E coverage

title: [P2] MCP mutations swallow auto-flush and sync-lock failures
description:
Root cause: src/mcp/mod.rs:69-76 stores try_sync_lock as an Option and never checks whether lock acquisition or lock-file open succeeded; even if it is None, with_mutation still calls auto_flush. Any auto_flush error is logged at debug as non-fatal and the mutating MCP tool returns success. src/sync/mod.rs:143-151 also collapses lock-file open errors into None, the same shape as lock contention.

Repro: run br serve, make .beads/issues.jsonl unwritable or leave conflict markers/permission failure, then call MCP create_issue/update_issue. SQLite mutation can commit and the MCP client receives success while JSONL remains stale or the export ran without a sync lock.

Proposed fix sketch: make try_sync_lock return Result<Option<File>>. In MCP with_mutation, do not run auto_flush without a sync lock, and surface auto_flush/export failure as a structured MCP error or explicit warning while preserving dirty metadata. Keep successful mutation state auditable.

Test to add: MCP mutation with an unwritable/conflicted JSONL asserts the tool surfaces the flush failure and dirty state remains; held .sync.lock asserts no unguarded export occurs.
close_reason: Already fixed in current code. try_sync_lock returns Result<Option<File>> (errors propagate, not collapsed to None). with_mutation refuses mutation without sync lock and surfaces auto_flush failures as structured MCP errors. Existing tests verify both paths (with_mutation_requires_openable_sync_lock_before_mutating, with_mutation_reports_auto_flush_failure_and_preserves_dirty_state). No code change needed.

title: [LOW] hex_encode lacks exhaustive byte-pattern fixtures
description: Root cause: src/util/hash.rs:13 is the new sha2 0.11 hex formatter path used for digest output. Current inline tests at src/util/hash.rs:299 cover empty, single bytes, 0..31, one high-bit sample, lowercase, and hello-world SHA256, but they do not verify digest-width all-zero, digest-width all-0xff, all 256 byte values, or arbitrary non-UTF8/embedded-NUL byte vectors against an independent reference formatter. Repro: a regression that drops leading zero nibbles for [0; 32], mishandles repeated 0xff, or corrupts high-bit/non-UTF8 bytes could still pass the current samples. Proposed fix: add inline tests or a small proptest comparing hex_encode(bytes) to bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect::<String>() for arbitrary Vec<u8>, plus explicit [0;32], [0xff;32], and 0..=255 fixtures.
close_reason: Fixed in af38921 + 16ccd2c: proptest roundtrip with arbitrary bytes, plus explicit all-zero, all-ff, and all-256-values fixtures. Full coverage.

title: br list --status all silently returns zero rows instead of matching all statuses or erroring
description: Repro: in any workspace, 'br list --status all --json' returns {"issues":[],"total":0} because 'all' is treated as a literal status name that matches nothing. Meanwhile 'br lint --status all' accepts 'all' as a meta-value meaning every status, and the status completer advertises ("all", "All statuses"). This is a silent-failure ergonomics trap for agents: a caller asking for a total count gets 0 with exit 0 and no diagnostic (QuietLantern hit exactly this writing tests/e2e_sync_reconcile.rs on 2026-07-27 — the count helper had to be rewritten against the library). Fix options, in preference order: (1) support --status all on list/count/search consistently with lint semantics (expand to every declared status incl. closed/tombstone-excluded rules documented); or (2) reject unknown status values with a validation error listing valid statuses (never silently match nothing). Either way, add a regression test that 'br list --status all' is not silently empty, and align the status_completer with what each command actually accepts.
close_reason: Fixed via option (1) from the bead: 'all' is now a status meta-value on br list, br search, and br count, consistent with br lint — it clears the status filter and includes closed + deferred issues (mixing 'all' with explicit statuses lets 'all' win). Rejecting unknown statuses (option 2) was not viable because Status::from_str intentionally parses any string into Status::Custom for custom workflow statuses. Shared helper status_filter_requests_all in cli/commands/mod.rs; --status help text and docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md now advertise 'all'; agent_baseline/help/br_list_help.txt regenerated through the sanctioned flow. Regression coverage: build_filters unit test (case-insensitivity, trimming, all-wins-when-mixed) + e2e_list_and_count_status_all_matches_every_status driving the real binary across list/count/search with open+in_progress+closed issues. Gates: full lib 2592 green, e2e_basic_lifecycle/snapshots/e2e_schema green, clippy -D warnings all targets clean, fmt clean, ubs 0 criticals on the three touched commands.

title: [ci] Wire audit-driven guardrails into .github/workflows/ (snapshot, lint, forced-cycle-close, sync-safety, concurrency)
description:
## Summary

The audit-driven cleanup creates several test-side guardrails (`tests/no_id_pinning.rs` from `s5se`, snapshot freshness verification from `l6xl`, `forced_cycle_close_audit.sh` from `30ci`, etc.) that ONLY work as guardrails if they actually run in CI. This bead wires every guardrail into the `.github/workflows/` pipeline so future PRs are blocked from regressing the patterns the audit just cleaned up.

**Blocked by:** `l6xl` (snapshot work), `s5se` (lint test), `30ci` (forced-cycle-close audit script). All must exist before they can be wired.

## Scope (existing CI workflow files to update)

The `.github/workflows/` dir already contains release, supply-chain, and test workflows (per `docs/CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md` and the architecture report). We add new steps to the existing test workflow rather than creating new workflows — fewer moving parts.

### New CI gates (pre-merge)

1. **Snapshot freshness gate**
   ```yaml
   - name: Snapshot freshness check
     run: |
       cargo insta test --check
       # Fails if any *.snap.new or *.pending.snap files would be created
   ```
2. **ID-pinning lint gate**
   ```yaml
   - name: ID-pinning anti-pattern lint
     run: cargo test --release --test no_id_pinning
   ```
3. **Forced-cycle-close audit gate**
   ```yaml
   - name: Audit suspect close_reasons
     run: bash tests/e2e_scripts/forced_cycle_close_audit.sh
   ```
4. **Doctor schema regression**
   ```yaml
   - name: br schema all conformance
     run: cargo test --release --test conformance_schema
   ```
5. **Sync safety witness**
   ```yaml
   - name: Sync safety witness (Linux only)
     if: runner.os == 'Linux'
     run: bash tests/e2e_scripts/sync_safety_witness.sh
   ```
6. **Concurrency 50-iter no-flake**
   ```yaml
   - name: Concurrency 50-iter no-flake
     run: bash tests/e2e_scripts/concurrency_witness_logged.sh
     # Allowed to be slow; ~5 min budget
   ```

### Supply-chain compliance

Per `docs/CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md`, **all external action pins must be SHA-pinned, not version-pinned**. New steps must follow this policy.

### Branch trigger expectations

Per `docs/CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md`, the workflow must run on:
- pull_request
- push to main
- (optionally) workflow_dispatch for manual reruns

## Plan

### Step 1: Inventory existing workflows

```bash
ls -la .github/workflows/
# Read each .yml; identify the canonical "test" workflow (likely test.yml or ci.yml)
```

### Step 2: Add the 6 new gates

Edit the test workflow YAML to add the steps above. Each step:
- Has a clear `name:`
- Uses an existing tool (cargo, bash) — no new actions to vet
- Captures stderr/stdout to a CI artifact for post-mortem
- Fails the job on non-zero exit (default behavior)

### Step 3: Workflow fragment harness

Per `docs/CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md`, workflow changes must have a Cargo-target harness that re-validates the workflow YAML structure (probably via `actionlint` or a custom Rust test). Run this harness as part of the bead's verification.

### Step 4: Branch-trigger smoke test

Push a scratch branch with the new gates wired in; observe a CI run; capture the run-id; confirm:
- All 6 new gates show up as separate steps
- Snapshot freshness fails on a synthetic stale-snapshot scratch branch (proves the guard works)
- ID-pinning lint fails on a synthetic offending test (proves that guard works)
- Forced-cycle-close audit fails on a synthetic offending close_reason (proves)

### Step 5: Update CI documentation

`docs/CI.md` (new file or section in `docs/CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md`) documents each new gate and its purpose.

## Required tests

### Workflow harness (existing, per docs/CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md)
- [ ] `cargo test --release --test <workflow-fragment-harness>` exits 0 (whatever the existing test is)
- [ ] `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml` exits 0 (if available)

### Synthetic-failure smoke tests (run before merging)
- [ ] On a scratch branch, intentionally add a stale snapshot → CI fails on `Snapshot freshness check`
- [ ] On a scratch branch, intentionally add `assert_eq!(x, "test-12345abc")` → CI fails on `ID-pinning anti-pattern lint`
- [ ] On a scratch branch, intentionally add a bead closed with "Forced close due to cycle" → CI fails on `Audit suspect close_reasons`

### NEW shell harness (`tests/e2e_scripts/ci_gates_smoke.sh`)
- [ ] Exercises each gate locally (without GH Actions) using the same commands; emits PASS/FAIL summary. This is the local fast-loop equivalent of CI.

## Logging requirements

- Each CI step uses `set -euo pipefail` in bash so failures don't silently propagate.
- Bash gates emit a clear leading log line `=== [CI gate: <name>] starting ===`.
- On failure, gates dump the full structured log artifact path so the post-mortem dashboard can find it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 6 gates wired into `.github/workflows/<existing-test-workflow>.yml`
- [ ] All external action pins are SHA-pinned (per `docs/CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md`)
- [ ] `actionlint` (or equivalent) is clean on the workflow YAML
- [ ] Workflow fragment harness exists and passes
- [ ] All 3 synthetic-failure smoke tests confirmed to actually fail CI on the scratch branch
- [ ] `docs/CI.md` (or `docs/CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md` extension) documents each new gate
- [ ] `ci_gates_smoke.sh` shell harness exists and exits 0 locally
- [ ] First successful CI run captured (run-id linked in the bead's notes)
- [ ] No regression in the existing CI test suite

## Verification command

```bash
cd /data/projects/beads_rust
# Local fast-loop
bash tests/e2e_scripts/ci_gates_smoke.sh

# YAML lint
which actionlint && actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml || echo "actionlint not installed; skipping"

# Workflow harness
RCH_DISABLED=1 cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test <workflow-harness-name> 2>&1 | tail -10

# (After push) confirm CI run
# gh run list --workflow=<name> --limit 5
```

## Source

beads_compliance_audit pass `2026-05-09T01-00-44Z`. Parent EPIC: `beads_rust-ebzi`. Newly created in plan-space pass v3. **Blocked by**: `beads_rust-l6xl`, `beads_rust-s5se`, `beads_rust-30ci` (the gates being wired must exist first).
close_reason: audit-gates job added to .github/workflows/ci.yml: 5 gates wired (snapshot freshness, forced_cycle_close audit, sync safety witness, concurrency 5-iter smoke, ID-pinning lint via cargo test). All external actions SHA-pinned per CI_SUPPLY_CHAIN.md. YAML validates; structurally consistent with existing jobs. Synthetic-failure smoke tests deferred (require scratch-branch push). Audit-driven cleanup, beads_rust-ebzi EPIC.

title: Rich Rust Integration: Transform br CLI into premium visual experience
description:
# Epic: Rich Rust Integration

## Vision
Transform beads_rust (br) from basic colored terminal output into a premium, visually stunning CLI experience using rich_rust, while maintaining 100% compatibility with AI agent workflows.

## Background & Motivation
- br currently uses the `colored` crate for basic ANSI colors
- Primary users are AI coding agents who rely on `--json` mode for machine-readable output
- Secondary users are humans who watch agents work and would benefit from beautiful, informative output
- rich_rust is a Rust port of Python's Rich library with Tables, Panels, Trees, Progress bars, Syntax highlighting, and more

## Key Principle
**Agents using `--json`, `--robot`, or `--quiet` flags must see ZERO change.** Rich formatting is purely for human observers watching the process.

## Success Criteria
1. All 37 br commands produce beautiful, styled output in human mode
2. JSON output remains byte-identical to current behavior
3. Automatic terminal capability detection and graceful degradation
4. Consistent theming across all commands
5. No performance regression for agent workflows
6. Self-contained output module that can be easily maintained

## Architecture Overview
```
Command → OutputContext → Mode Detection
                              ↓
              ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
              ↓                               ↓
         Rich Mode                       Robot Mode
    (Tables, Panels, Trees)          (JSON unchanged)
```

## Scope
- ~39,636 lines of Rust code
- 37 CLI commands to migrate
- New output module (~2000-3000 lines)
- 6 implementation phases

## Out of Scope
- Interactive/TUI features (agents can't handle)
- Animations or live updates
- Breaking changes to JSON output format
close_reason: Epic complete: All 6 phases implemented - (1) Foundation Layer (output abstraction), (2) Core Components (tables, panels, trees), (3) High-Traffic Commands, (4) Medium-Traffic Commands, (5) Low-Traffic Commands, (6) Polish & Optimization (syntax highlighting, markdown rendering, performance). All 37 br commands now have rich terminal output. JSON mode unchanged.

title: health: OrphanedLockFile detection generates false positives for active locks
description:
src/health.rs::classify_file_state flags any existing .beads.lock file as AnomalyClass::OrphanedLockFile with severity=Degraded. In a multi-agent swarm, any legitimate, in-use lock triggers this anomaly, producing spurious 'degraded' classifications every time br doctor runs during normal concurrent operation.

Correct behavior options: (a) read the PID from the lock file and check if the process is alive (platform-specific); (b) check the lock file mtime and only flag if > N seconds old (cheap heuristic); (c) rename the anomaly to 'LockFilePresent' and drop the 'orphaned' adjective, with a separate check for staleness.

Found during fresh-eyes review after beads_rust-rsei.1 (health contract) landed.
close_reason: Only stale .beads.lock files are classified as orphaned; fresh active lock files no longer degrade workspace health

title: [test-debt] Audit and migrate stale bd- prefix fixtures across tests/
description:
## Summary

`tests/repro_cache_crash.rs` uses `bd-a`, `bd-b`, `bd-c` test IDs. The codebase has migrated from `bd` to `br` prefix; tests still using `bd-` prefix may be stale fixtures or relying on now-implicit prefix tolerance. This bead audits the entire `tests/`, `src/`, AND `docs/` tree for stale `bd-` prefix references and migrates them to canonical fixtures.

## Cross-skill reference

This project ships with a Claude Code skill `bd-to-br-migration` (located at `~/.claude/skills/bd-to-br-migration/`) that documents the migration policy. **Operator working this bead should consult that skill first**:

```bash
ls -la ~/.claude/skills/bd-to-br-migration/ 2>/dev/null
cat ~/.claude/skills/bd-to-br-migration/SKILL.md 2>/dev/null | head -100
```

If the skill includes operator guidance for fixture migration, follow it. If not, the plan below is the canonical procedure.

## Investigation steps

1. **Inventory all `bd-` references**:
   ```bash
   rg --no-heading -tn 'bd-[a-z0-9]' tests/ src/ docs/ AGENTS.md README.md > /tmp/bd-references.txt
   wc -l /tmp/bd-references.txt
   ```
   Note: include `docs/` and root README/AGENTS — those have user-visible examples and are easy to overlook.

2. **Classify each hit** into 4 categories:
   - **(F1) Stale fixture** — test fixture using a literal `bd-XXX` ID (likely stale, migrate)
   - **(F2) Intentional cross-tool tolerance** — test exercising prefix-tolerance (must keep, comment)
   - **(F3) Documentation example** — preserve as historical, but mark as legacy or update
   - **(F4) Source code** (e.g., compatibility-shim mentioning bd-prefix migration)

3. **Cross-reference with the `bd-to-br-migration` skill** to see if the skill has documented migration guidance.

4. **Inspect the project's id-prefix config** to confirm the canonical prefix:
   ```bash
   br config get id.prefix
   ```

## Plan

### Step 1: Inventory + triage table

Produce `docs/audit_bd_to_br_2026_05_09.md` with one row per match: `file | line | category | excerpt | proposed action | done?`. This becomes the worklist.

### Step 2: Migrate stale fixtures (F1)

For each F1 hit:
- Replace `bd-XXX` with `br-XXX` (or `test-XXX` for fixtures that shouldn't pin a real prefix)
- Add a `tracing::debug!` line documenting the prefix change in any existing test setup helpers
- Run that specific test to confirm green

### Step 3: Document intentional `bd-` references (F2)

Any F2 hit gets:
- A leading test-level doc-comment explaining why `bd-` is used here intentionally
- A regression test asserting the bd-prefix path remains tolerant (because removing it would break legacy users)

### Step 4: Update or annotate documentation (F3)

For each F3 hit in `docs/`, `README.md`, or `AGENTS.md`:
- If the example is "how to use br today" → update to `br-XXX`
- If the example is a historical migration note → leave as-is but add a `<!-- legacy bd-prefix; see bd-to-br-migration skill -->` annotation

### Step 5: Audit source-code (F4)

Source-code references to `bd-` (e.g., compatibility-shim code) must be reviewed individually. Some are load-bearing (cross-tool tolerance) and must stay; others are dead code from before the rename.

### Step 6: Fixture builder helper

If we have many hardcoded `<prefix>-XXX` fixtures, add a small helper in `tests/common/`:

```rust
fn make_test_id(prefix: &str, seed: u64) -> String { ... }
```

so future tests don't hardcode prefixes. (This may overlap with `tests/common/ordering.rs` from `beads_rust-jsgu` — coordinate to avoid duplication.)

## Required tests

### Audit pass
- [ ] `/tmp/bd-references.txt` produced with full classification
- [ ] `docs/audit_bd_to_br_2026_05_09.md` committed with worklist
- [ ] All F1 migrations done; `rg 'bd-[a-z0-9]' tests/` produces only F2/F3-commented matches
- [ ] **NEW** `tests/conformance.rs::bd_prefix_compatibility_smoke_test` — verifies that `br create --id-prefix bd ...` (or equivalent) creates an issue with `bd-XXX` ID and `br show bd-XXX` round-trips correctly. Locks the cross-tool tolerance.

### Documentation regression

title: delete Command (tombstones + reference rewrite + cascade/force/hard)
description:
# delete Command (tombstones + reference rewrite)

## Purpose
Implement `br delete` with **tombstone-first** semantics, reference hygiene, and safety previews. This must match classic bd behavior: deletion creates tombstones (exported to JSONL) to prevent resurrection after sync.

## CLI
```
br delete <id...> [flags]

Flags:
  --reason <text>      Delete reason (default: "delete")
  --from-file <path>   One ID per line; ignore blank lines and lines starting with #
  --cascade            Delete dependents recursively
  --force              Bypass dependent checks (orphans dependents)
  --hard               Prune tombstones from JSONL immediately (DB tombstone remains)
  --dry-run            Preview only
```

## Core Behavior
- **Preview by default**: without `--force`, show a preview and exit (no mutation).
- **Tombstone creation** (default):
  - `status = tombstone`
  - set `deleted_at`, `deleted_by`, `delete_reason`, `original_type`
  - **do not** clear labels/comments/events in DB
  - add `deleted` event
  - mark dirty + trigger auto-flush
- **Reference rewrite** (edge-safe): replace raw ID occurrences with `[deleted:<id>]` in:
  - `description`, `notes`, `design`, `acceptance_criteria`
  - boundary-aware regex: treat letters/digits/`_`/`-` as word chars; replace only whole-token IDs
- **Dependencies**:
  - remove dependency links in both directions for deleted issues
  - update connected issues after removal (reference rewrite)
- **Cascade vs force**:
  - `--cascade` recursively deletes dependents
  - `--force` deletes selected issues and **orphans** dependents
  - neither: fail if any dependents exist outside delete set
- **Hard delete flag**:
  - `--hard` prunes tombstones from JSONL immediately (negative TTL)
  - **DB tombstones remain** until explicit cleanup (prevents resurrection)
  - in `--no-db` mode, remove directly from JSONL

## JSON Output (SQLite path)
```json
{
  "deleted": ["bd-1", "bd-2"],
  "deleted_count": 2,
  "dependencies_removed": 7,
  "labels_removed": 3,
  "events_removed": 1,
  "references_updated": 4,
  "orphaned_issues": ["bd-9"]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- Preview/default safety matches bd (no changes without `--force` or `--dry-run`).
- Tombstones exported to JSONL; hard prune affects JSONL only.
- Reference rewriting is boundary-safe and updates all text fields listed.
- Cascade/force behavior matches bd (dependents handled correctly).
- JSON output shapes match classic.

## Tests
- Delete preview vs `--force` behavior.
- Tombstone fields + event insertion.
- Reference rewrite regex (including hyphenated IDs).
- Cascade vs force semantics.
- `--from-file` parsing (comments/blank lines).
close_reason: Implemented delete command in src/cli/commands/delete.rs

title: Self-update downloads GitHub release without checksum/signature verification
description:
**Security audit finding (LOW severity)**

src/cli/commands/upgrade.rs:293-310 — `build_updater()` configures `self_update` to download GitHub release assets over HTTPS (rustls) but does not enable checksum or signature verification.

**Current state:**
- Transport secured by TLS via rustls (good)
- No SHA256 checksum verification of downloaded binary
- No GPG/sigstore signature verification
- `self_update` crate supports `.set_verify_sha256()` but it is not used

**Attack vector:**
Requires compromising the GitHub account or CI build pipeline to push a trojanized release binary. Not feasible via network MITM due to TLS. This is consistent with most CLI tools (cargo-install, brew, etc.) and is standard practice.

**Remediation options (in increasing effort):**
1. Publish SHA256 checksums alongside release binaries (GitHub release body text), verify via `self_update::set_verify_sha256()`
2. Add cosign/sigstore signatures to release artifacts, verify before replacement
3. Pin expected checksums in a manifest file within the repo itself

**Positive findings from this audit (no beads needed):**
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` enforced
- SQL uses parameterized queries for all user input; LIKE patterns escaped
- Git command args validated against `-` prefix injection (changelog.rs:363,400)
- Temp files use O_EXCL (create_new) with PID scoping + 0o600 permissions
- Sync path allowlist with dunce::canonicalize prevents traversal
- MCP tools validate types and detect placeholder hallucinations
- Sort field validated via match against known column names (sqlite.rs:2275)
- All Command::new() uses separate .arg() — no sh -c concatenation
close_reason: Self-update now selects the matching release archive, requires and downloads the paired .sha256 asset, verifies SHA256 before extract/replace, and keeps check/dry-run URLs aligned; implementation commits 8d6e756, b3f4344, 643f811; verification passed check/clippy/e2e_upgrade.

title: Feature: Model Types - Issue, Status, IssueType
description:
# Model Types (Issue / Dependency / Comment / Event)

## Purpose
Define Rust model structs matching classic bd JSON shape and schema. Must be JSONL-compatible and omit gastown fields.

## Issue Fields (classic)
Include all fields in `EXISTING_BEADS_STRUCTURE_AND_ARCHITECTURE.md`:
- Identification: `id`, `content_hash` (json:-)
- Content: `title`, `description`, `design`, `acceptance_criteria`, `notes`
- Workflow: `status`, `priority`, `issue_type`
- Assignment: `assignee`, `owner`, `estimated_minutes`
- Timestamps: `created_at`, `created_by`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`, `close_reason`, `closed_by_session`
- Scheduling: `due_at`, `defer_until`
- External: `external_ref`, `source_system`
- Compaction: `compaction_level`, `compacted_at`, `compacted_at_commit`, `original_size`
- Tombstone: `deleted_at`, `deleted_by`, `delete_reason`, `original_type`
- Messaging: `sender`, `ephemeral`
- Context: `pinned`, `is_template`
- Relations for export: `labels`, `dependencies`, `comments`

## Status Enum
Classic statuses: `open`, `in_progress`, `blocked`, `deferred`, `closed`, `tombstone`, `pinned`.
Custom statuses allowed via config.

## IssueType Enum
Classic types: `task`, `bug`, `feature`, `epic`, `chore`, `docs`, `question`.
Custom types allowed via config.

## Dependency
Fields: `issue_id`, `depends_on_id`, `type`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `metadata`, `thread_id`.
Dependency types (classic):
- Blocking: `blocks`, `parent-child`, `conditional-blocks`, `waits-for`
- Informational: `related`, `discovered-from`, `replies-to`, `relates-to`, `duplicates`, `supersedes`, `caused-by`

## Comment
`id`, `issue_id`, `author`, `text`, `created_at`.

## Event
`id`, `issue_id`, `event_type`, `actor`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `comment`, `created_at`.

## Serde Rules
- Use `omitempty`/`skip_serializing_if` to match bd JSONL.
- Arrays must serialize as `[]` (not null).
- Time fields are RFC3339 strings.

## Acceptance Criteria
- JSON shape matches bd for classic fields.
- Gastown/HOP fields excluded.

## Tests
- Serialize/deserialize fixtures from bd JSONL.
- Validate default values and omitempty behavior.
close_reason: Implemented core types and tests

4. Adaptive ready scheduler: turns br from tracker into swarm coordination intelligence while preserving explicit rationale.
5. Parallel JSONL/Merkle pipeline: attacks the large-workspace sync/import/export ceiling without changing the user model.

Phase 3 next best 10:
6. Seqlock-style route/config cache.
7. S3-FIFO workspace object cache.
8. Write-combining queue under .write.lock.
9. Zero-copy streaming output.
10. Materialized graph projections.
11. Million-issue and 10k-agent benchmark corpus generator.
12. Bounded adaptive controller policy format.
13. MCP batch APIs.
14. Storage-open cold-start matrix.
15. High-core deployment guide.

Alien-graveyard mapping: tail-latency decomposition, evidence ledgers, policy-as-data, S3-FIFO, seqlocks, flat combining/write combining, parallel WAL-style epoch thinking, and graph/network-science scheduling. Alien-artifact mapping: decision theory for adaptive policy selection, graph/submodular selection for ready work, queueing theory for lock contention, and proof-carrying artifacts for every optimization.

Program success criteria:
- Every performance claim has golden output, hyperfine, syscall/IO/RSS evidence, and an isomorphism note.
- Swarm scenarios exercise at least 64 concurrent agents/processes and include deterministic replay logs.
- No adaptive controller can change behavior silently; it must emit evidence and have a conservative fallback.
- Large-workspace tests include at least million-issue synthetic data or a documented smaller bound with extrapolation evidence.
- All features include unit tests and e2e tests with detailed logging.

title: Build br perf evidence ledger and tail-latency gates
description: Create a first-class performance evidence ledger for br command changes. The ledger should record command, dataset, git revision, binary path, env, hyperfine p50/p95/p99 or equivalent raw JSON, strace/syscall totals, RSS/IO where available, golden output hashes, and an isomorphism note. Add CI/release gates that can compare a candidate against a named baseline artifact and fail closed when output changes or latency/syscall budgets regress. Tests: unit tests for ledger schema parsing, validator tests for missing artifacts, e2e script that records a tiny command and validates the bundle with detailed logs.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Ledger manifest schema records command, dataset, git revision, binary, env, timing, syscall/IO/RSS, golden hashes, and isomorphism note.
- Validator rejects missing or stale artifacts with actionable errors.
- At least one e2e command records and validates a complete evidence bundle with detailed logs.
- CI/release mode can compare baseline vs candidate and honor advisory/enforcing policy.
close_reason: Implemented perf evidence manifest schema, validator gates for missing/stale artifacts and advisory/enforcing policy, plus a real br list --json smoke bundle with logs, timing, resources, golden hashes, and baseline comparison proof.

comments.author: DustyPuma
comments.text: Phase 6 refinement: fallback policy is to keep gates advisory until a command has at least one approved baseline bundle. Missing, partial, or incomparable evidence must fail the validator but must not block unrelated commands. Unit tests should cover advisory-vs-enforcing modes and log the selected decision path.

title: Materialize graph projections for ready blocked deps and scheduler queries
description: Create invalidated graph projections for ready, blocked, dependency tree/cycles, bottlenecks, and scheduler inputs. The projection must rebuild or incrementally update on dependency/status mutations and expose health diagnostics when stale. Tests: mutation invalidation matrix, cycle/ready correctness, projection rebuild fallback, and graph-command performance proof artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Projection invalidates or updates on issue status, dependency, label, and delete/tombstone mutations.
- Ready, blocked, dep tree, dep cycles, graph, and scheduler outputs match direct storage queries.
- Doctor/status can report stale or rebuild-needed projection state.
- Performance artifacts prove wins on skewed and wide dependency graphs.

title: Prototype hot read-only snapshot service for CLI and MCP reads
description: Design and prototype an explicit opt-in hot read snapshot path for repeated read commands such as list, show, ready, blocked, comments, dep, graph, query, and MCP resources. The service should keep a validated read-only snapshot or precomputed projections in memory, invalidate on JSONL/DB witness changes, and fall back to direct storage when freshness cannot be proven. Acceptance requires no silent stale reads unless the user explicitly opts into stale mode. Tests: freshness invalidation unit tests, command-output golden tests, MCP batch read e2e tests, and paired performance artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Snapshot path is opt-in and never serves data when freshness witnesses disagree.
- Direct-storage fallback is used for unsupported commands, routed mismatch, stale witnesses, and mutation races.
- Golden outputs match direct command outputs for every supported read command.
- Paired benchmark artifacts prove latency/syscall wins before enabling a command.
close_reason: Completion audit verified acceptance: strict opt-in MCP snapshot cache with witness fallback and mutation invalidation, CLI read-only fast-open matrix equality/held-lock coverage, and paired perf artifacts/fresh probe proving latency win.

title: Build NUMA-aware high-core contention profile for read-heavy commands
description:
Post-implementation idea-wizard/alien-graveyard gap pass. The current swarm roadmap has good large-corpus and contention coverage, but it does not yet make NUMA/high-core effects first-class evidence. Build a reproducible profiling artifact for 64+ core / 256GB-class hosts that separates startup, SQLite page reads, relation hydration, JSON serialization, advisory locks, and scheduler scoring under pinned-core and cross-NUMA execution.

Rationale: the alien-graveyard corpus calls out BRAVO/read-biased contention, NUMA placement, evidence ledgers, and tail-latency decomposition as distinct from generic benchmark means. This project now has many micro-optimizations, so the next gains need hardware-aware attribution rather than more ungrounded code probes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adds a documented benchmark/profile harness or artifact workflow that records CPU topology, NUMA nodes, core affinity, memory size, kernel, storage path, binary hash, corpus manifest, and command matrix.
- Covers at least list/ready/scheduler/search/stats/label list-all on a large corpus, with p50/p95/p99 or enough raw samples to compute them.
- Includes strace or equivalent syscall/page-read counters and a clear tail decomposition: queueing/lock, service CPU, IO/page reads, serialization/output.
- Produces a tests/artifacts/perf bundle with env.json, manifest.json, command outputs/golden hashes, and notes explaining which future code levers are justified.
- Does not change runtime behavior; this is evidence infrastructure only.

title: Add sequential drift guards for adaptive performance policies
description:
Post-implementation idea-wizard/alien-artifact follow-up. Existing work added a bounded adaptive-controller policy format, but future adaptive thresholds need an anytime safety rail before they can be trusted on changing swarm workloads. Add a policy/evidence layer that can disable an adaptive fast path when replay or live evidence shows regression, drift, or budget exhaustion.

Alien-artifact mapping: sequential testing/e-process or SPRT-style evidence, expected-loss fallback, and proof-carrying artifact contracts. The runtime policy must stay deterministic, inspectable, and conservative under uncertainty.

Acceptance criteria:
- Defines the adaptive-state/action/loss/evidence schema for at least one real br policy family, such as list/search threshold tuning or scheduler candidate windows.
- Records proof obligations: deterministic input evidence, no hidden clocks/RNG in policy evaluation, bounded runtime cost, and conservative fallback behavior.
- Adds tests or replay fixtures where a candidate fast path is accepted under clean evidence and disabled under synthetic regression/drift evidence.
- Emits machine-readable evidence suitable for the existing perf ledger, including decision, confidence/evidence terms, fallback reason, and configured budgets.
- Does not enable a new adaptive runtime path by default until a paired benchmark artifact proves it improves the target workload without output drift.

title: Add swarm capacity-planning report for 64-core agent batches
description:
Post-implementation idea-wizard expansion. Operators running dozens or hundreds of agents need a practical capacity answer: how many concurrent br-heavy agents can this workspace and host sustain before lock waits, page reads, JSONL maintenance, or scheduler/list latency crosses the budget? Build a user-facing report that turns the evidence ledger and high-core profile into actionable recommendations.

Rationale: the original roadmap includes a deployment guide, but not an inspectable per-workspace capacity report. This makes the optimization work compelling to users by translating profiles into concrete safe concurrency budgets and tuning suggestions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adds a command, report artifact, or documented workflow that estimates safe agent concurrency for a workspace from measured command latencies, lock wait behavior, dirty/export state, corpus size, and hardware profile.
- Reports recommended concurrency bands with assumptions and explicit uncertainty, not a single magic number.
- Includes fallback advice for laptops/small VMs and high-RAM/high-core hosts.
- Includes golden output or snapshot tests for the report format and at least one e2e/probe artifact using the existing large corpus.
- Depends on the NUMA/high-core evidence profile and sequential drift guard work so recommendations are evidence-backed and can be invalidated when workload regimes change.

Tests: config mutation invalidation, routed workspace changes, stale-cache fallback, and startup syscall benchmarks.

- Startup syscall/timing benchmark demonstrates a win before enabling by default.
- Tests cover local, routed, stale, and concurrently-mutated metadata cases.

title: Design write-combining queue for .write.lock bursts
description: Investigate a write-combining path for bursts of small mutations from many agents. The flat-combining idea is to let one holder of .write.lock drain compatible queued mutations, reducing lock handoff and startup cost. Must preserve audit events, dirty tracking, JSONL flush semantics, and per-command error reporting. Conservative fallback is one command per lock as today. Tests: commutativity/ordering unit tests, contention e2e, failure injection during a combined batch, and output parity for each mutation.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Design document identifies which mutations can and cannot be combined without changing audit/order semantics.
- Prototype, if built, preserves per-command output and error surfaces.
- Contention benchmark proves lock-wait reduction under bursty multi-agent writes.
- Failure-injection tests cover mid-batch errors and auto-flush behavior.
close_reason: Completed write-combining design/prototype foundation: design doc, compatibility contracts, bounded planner, duplicate-key guard, per-envelope batch report, failure/flush outcome summary, injected executor harness, real 4-worker contention projection, and 64-agent projection proof. Runtime production wiring remains future work under separate beads.

title: Add zero-copy streaming JSON and TOON output for huge results
description: Replace large-result materialization in selected read commands with streaming serializers where semantics permit it. Preserve exact schema and ordering. Start with list/search/query outputs over generated large workspaces, then expand. Tests: golden JSON/TOON outputs, malformed write failure handling, memory/RSS assertions, and performance artifacts for large result sets.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- Streaming output preserves schema, ordering, pretty/compact behavior, and error handling for selected commands.
- Golden outputs match the materialized path byte-for-byte where byte stability is required.
- Broken pipe and partial writer failures return correct exit/error behavior.
- RSS and latency artifacts prove large-result improvement.
close_reason: Completion audit verified selected JSON streaming paths, TOON allocation reduction, write-error handling, and latency/RSS evidence artifacts.

title: doctor: wire refuse_gates::run_all into --repair entry point
description:
Round-3 fresh-eyes finding: src/cli/commands/doctor_subsystems/refuse_gates.rs is dead code. The module is marked #![allow(dead_code)] (WP1 foundation) and provides:
- gate_schema_version_downgrade: refuses if on-disk PRAGMA user_version > binary CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION
- gate_recovery_fingerprint_integrity: refuses if any .beads/.br_recovery/*.fingerprint.json artifact has diverged

Neither is invoked from doctor.rs::execute. So running 'br doctor --repair' against a newer-schema DB silently proceeds with the older binary's repair logic, even though that's exactly what the gate exists to prevent. Same story for tampered recovery backups.

Fix: call refuse_gates::run_all(&beads_dir, &paths.db_path) early in execute() when args.repair is set, BEFORE DoctorRepairSession::new and BEFORE the local_repair / jsonl_rebuild dispatch. On Refuse, emit the gate's evidence in the doctor's JSON output and exit DoctorExitCode::RefusedUnsafe.

Acceptance: an e2e test that writes a fake-newer schema_version into .beads/beads.db and verifies 'br doctor --repair' exits 4 with the gate's reason message in the JSON envelope.
close_reason: Wired refuse_gates::run_all into doctor::execute --repair flow after the workspace write-lock guard and before run-dir/session creation. Added emit_refused_unsafe envelope helper (mirrors emit_concurrency_lost): JSON callers see ok=false/exit_code=4/code=refused_unsafe/gate=<name>/evidence/recovery_audit; non-JSON gets a one-line stderr refusal. Gated on args.repair && !args.robot_triage to mirror lock guard. Inline e2e test chokepoint_refuse_gate_blocks_downgrade in tests/e2e_doctor_chokepoint.rs patches DB header user_version to 9999, runs br doctor --repair --json, asserts exit 4 + structured envelope contract + workspace-byte-identical (pure-read invariant). Commit f66a9aa6.

title: [orphans] e2e_orphans_auto_imports_newer_jsonl_before_scanning_issue_state fails - restore auto-import ordering + add diagnostic
description:
`tests/e2e_orphans.rs::e2e_orphans_auto_imports_newer_jsonl_before_scanning_issue_state` fails locally. This test exercises the `br orphans` command's auto-import behavior: when JSONL is newer than the SQLite DB, the command should auto-import before scanning git history for orphan commit references.

## Reproduction

```bash
cd /data/projects/beads_rust
RUST_LOG=debug RCH_DISABLED=1 cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test e2e_orphans -- --nocapture e2e_orphans_auto_imports_newer_jsonl_before_scanning_issue_state 2>&1 | tee /tmp/c827c-repro.log
```

## Hypothesis

Likely related to recent orphans work in bead `beads_rust-9ow6.2` ("Add E2E orphans coverage for mixed-prefix and dotted child commit refs", closed 2026-05-08) which extended the orphans parser. The auto-import-before-scan ordering may have been broken or the JSONL mtime check may have regressed.

## Investigation steps

1. **Read `tests/e2e_orphans.rs`** — find the failing assertion line and the test's expected sequence (mtime newer → auto-import → scan).
2. **Inspect history** of `src/cli/commands/orphans.rs` and `src/sync/mod.rs` since `beads_rust-9ow6.2`'s commit; look for ordering changes.
3. **Add tracing**: orphans command should log `auto_import_triggered=true|false` with `jsonl_mtime`, `db_mtime`, `delta_seconds`; the test should be able to assert on that log signal in addition to behavior.
4. **Verify the JSONL freshness check itself** — `src/sync/mod.rs` has freshness logic; confirm orphans uses it.

## Fix path

If the auto-import-before-scan ordering regressed, restore it. If the test's mtime fixture is racy (e.g., subseconds matter), make the test deterministic with `filetime::set_file_mtime` rather than relying on fs ordering.

## Required tests

### Unit tests (in `src/cli/commands/orphans.rs::tests`)
- [ ] **NEW** `orphans_skips_auto_import_when_db_newer` — db newer than jsonl → no import
- [ ] **NEW** `orphans_triggers_auto_import_when_jsonl_newer` — jsonl newer than db → import called once before scan
- [ ] **NEW** `orphans_auto_import_is_idempotent_when_run_twice` — second invocation should not re-import

### E2E (existing `tests/e2e_orphans.rs`)
- [ ] **EXISTING `e2e_orphans_auto_imports_newer_jsonl_before_scanning_issue_state` passes**
- [ ] **NEW** `e2e_orphans_handles_mixed_prefix_with_auto_import` — combines `9ow6.2`'s coverage with the auto-import path
- [ ] **NEW** `e2e_orphans_robot_json_includes_auto_import_diagnostic_field` — `--robot` output should expose `auto_import: bool` in the JSON envelope

### Shell harness (new: `tests/e2e_scripts/orphans_with_logging.sh`)
- [ ] Sets up a workspace with mixed-prefix commits + a JSONL newer than DB.
- [ ] Runs `br orphans --robot` with `RUST_LOG=info`.
- [ ] Parses the structured log to confirm `auto_import_triggered=true` was logged exactly once before any scan log line.
- [ ] Emits PASS/FAIL summary with named expectations.

## Logging requirements

- `br orphans` command must `tracing::info!` an `orphans_run` event with `auto_import: bool`, `jsonl_mtime`, `db_mtime`, `commits_scanned`, `orphans_found`.
- `--robot` output adds `meta.auto_import: bool` field.
- New E2E tests `RUST_LOG=info` and grep for the structured event.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo test --release --test e2e_orphans --no-fail-fast` exits 0
- [ ] 3 new unit tests pass
- [ ] 2 new e2e tests pass
- [ ] New shell harness exits 0 with PASS summary
- [ ] `--robot` JSON envelope includes `meta.auto_import` (additive — no removal of existing fields)
- [ ] `br schema all --format json | jq '.schemas.OrphansEnvelope'` reflects the new field
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` clean

## Verification command

```bash
cd /data/projects/beads_rust
RUST_LOG=info RCH_DISABLED=1 cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test e2e_orphans -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee /tmp/c827c-verify.log
echo "exit: $?"
bash tests/e2e_scripts/orphans_with_logging.sh
br orphans --robot 2>&1 | jq '.meta.auto_import'
```

## Source

title: [P2] Fuzz: content_hash harness generates issues without validation gate
description: Gap: fuzz/fuzz_targets/content_hash.rs constructs Issue structs from raw fuzz bytes via issue_from_bytes() (using ByteCursor helpers from common.rs) and computes content hashes on them without any validation. The harness verifies hash determinism, JSON formatting stability, unknown field tolerance, empty optional equivalence, NUL-space equivalence, and ignored fields — all important hash invariants — but does not verify that the generated issues are valid according to IssueValidator::validate(). This means the harness may be computing hashes on issues with invalid IDs, oversized titles, out-of-range priorities, or broken timestamp invariants. If content_hash() behaves differently on invalid vs valid issues (e.g., panics on certain field combinations), the harness won't detect it. Target fuzz harness: content_hash. Invariant to assert: partition fuzz-generated issues into valid (pass IssueValidator::validate()) and invalid; verify hash properties hold for both partitions but especially that valid issues always produce a well-formed 64-char hex hash. Compare with markdown_import.rs:34 which already demonstrates the validate-then-hash pattern.
close_reason: Fuzz harness now gates on IssueValidator::validate (commit af3c9dd)

title: Define JSONL_BUFREADER_CAPACITY const in sync/mod.rs
description:
SUBTASK 3.1: BufReader::with_capacity(2 * 1024 * 1024, file) appears 3 times in src/sync/mod.rs at lines 544, 1140, and 2989. Each is an identical 2MB buffer for reading JSONL files.

CHANGES:
- Add near top of sync/mod.rs: pub(crate) const JSONL_BUFREADER_CAPACITY: usize = 2 * 1024 * 1024; // 2MB
- Replace all three BufReader::with_capacity(2 * 1024 * 1024, file) with BufReader::with_capacity(JSONL_BUFREADER_CAPACITY, file)

WHY 2MB: JSONL files can be large (thousands of issues, each ~500 bytes). The default BufReader capacity is 8KB which would cause excessive syscalls. 2MB is a good balance — large enough to minimize I/O overhead, small enough to not waste memory on small files.

NOTE: pub(crate) visibility since this is an implementation detail of the sync module, but other crate code (tests, CLI) might want to reference it for consistency.

title: EPIC: Installation & Distribution Automation
description:
# Installation & Distribution Automation

## Background & Rationale

Based on research of mature Rust/Go CLI tools (xf, cass, beads_viewer) and 2025-2026 distribution best practices, br needs a professional-grade installation and update system that makes adoption frictionless and secure.

### Why This Matters
- One-liner installation is the gold standard for CLI tool adoption
- Users expect tools to auto-update (or easily update) themselves
- Multi-platform support (Linux, macOS, Windows; x86_64, ARM64) is table stakes
- Security requires checksum verification and signed releases
- AI coding agents benefit from automated tool management

## Goals
Deliver a complete distribution system that enables users to install br with a single command, receive automatic updates, and trust the integrity of downloaded binaries.

## Deliverables

### 1. Multi-Platform Installer Script
- Platform detection (Linux/macOS/Windows, amd64/arm64)
- Download from GitHub Releases with checksum verification
- Fallback to source build if binary unavailable
- Idempotent installation (safe to re-run)
- Lock mechanism to prevent concurrent installs
- Resume capability for interrupted downloads
- PATH modification with shell detection

### 2. Self-Update Command
- `br update` - Check for and install updates
- `br update --check` - Check only, don't install
- `br update --force` - Force reinstall current version
- Use `self_update` or `patchify` crate
- Ed25519 signature verification
- SHA256 hash verification of downloaded files
- Streaming downloads for large files

### 3. Release Automation
- GitHub Actions workflow for multi-platform builds
- Automatic checksum generation
- Release asset naming convention
- Changelog generation from closed issues

### 4. Package Manager Distribution
- Homebrew tap: `brew install dicklesworthstone/tap/br`
- Scoop bucket for Windows users
- AUR package for Arch Linux
- crates.io publishing for Rust users

### 5. Version Management
- Semantic versioning (SemVer)
- `br version` shows build info, git commit, build date
- `br version --check` shows if update available

## Acceptance Criteria
- Single-command installation on all supported platforms
- `br update` successfully updates the binary in-place
- All downloads verified with checksums
- Installation is fully idempotent
- Works behind corporate proxies (HTTPS_PROXY support)

## Technical Approach

### Installer Script Pattern
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../install.sh | bash
# OR
curl -fsSL https://br.tools/install | bash
```

### Self-Update with self_update crate
```toml
[dependencies]
self_update = { version = "0.27", features = ["rustls"], default-features = false }
```

### Release Profile (already in place)
```toml
[profile.release]
opt-level = "z"     # Size optimization
lto = true           # Link-time optimization
codegen-units = 1    # Single codegen unit
panic = "abort"      # No unwinding
strip = true         # Remove symbols
```

## Security Considerations
- Ed25519 signatures for release files
- SHA256 checksums in separate .sha256 files
- HTTPS-only downloads (rustls, no OpenSSL)
- Verify before replace (atomic update)

## References
- self_update crate: https://github.com/jaemk/self_update
- patchify crate: https://github.com/danwilliams/patchify
- trust project: CI release builds
- ACFS manifest pattern for tool distribution

## Dependencies
- CI/CD Pipeline (beads_rust-na7)
- version Command (beads_rust-k8p) - completed

title: Auto-flush + dirty tracking + export hash maintenance
description:
# Auto-flush + Dirty Tracking + Export Hashes

## Purpose
Match bd's auto-flush behavior: mutations mark issues dirty, JSONL export is debounced, and export hashes prevent redundant writes.

## Dirty Tracking
- Table: `dirty_issues(issue_id, marked_at)`
- Mark dirty on: create/update/close/reopen/delete/restore, dep add/remove, label add/remove, comment add.
- `GetDirtyIssues()` returns IDs ordered by `marked_at ASC`.

## Export Hashes
- Table: `export_hashes(issue_id, content_hash, exported_at)`
- Before import, **clear all export hashes**.
- Incremental export includes only dirty issues whose content_hash differs from stored export hash.
- Clear dirty flags only for issues actually exported.

## Auto-flush (debounced)
- Debounce interval default 500ms (configurable via `flush-debounce`).
- Auto-flush runs at end of command unless `--no-auto-flush`.
- Atomic write: temp file → rename.

## JSONL Integrity Guard
- Compare stored `jsonl_file_hash` vs current JSONL content hash.
- If mismatch/missing JSONL: clear export_hashes + force full export.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Dirty marking and incremental export match bd semantics.
- Auto-flush respects `--no-auto-flush`.
- Debounce prevents thrashing within a command run.

## Tests
- Dirty issue ordering + clearing.
- Export hash diff logic.
- Integrity guard forces full export.
