title: Consolidate default ID prefix and misc scattered constants
description:
PARENT TASK 6 of 7: The default ID prefix "br" is hardcoded in 4 separate places: util/id.rs:29 (IdConfig::default), util/id.rs:506 (normalize_prefix), util/id.rs:575 (ResolverConfig::default), and config/mod.rs:1816 (default_config_layer). This means changing the default prefix requires finding and updating 4 locations.

Additionally, several other one-off constants are scattered without names: (1) config/mod.rs lines 231 and 463 both use 10 as the max redirect depth for follow_redirects(). (2) main.rs:333 uses ".sync.lock" as an advisory lock filename. (3) cli/mod.rs:464 uses 60 as the completion title truncation width. (4) output/components/dep_tree.rs:22 uses 10 as the default max tree depth. (5) cli/commands/sync.rs lines 443 and 751 both use 12 as the hash display truncation length.

Also in util/id.rs, the ID generation algorithm has several unnamed magic numbers: line 133 (10 nonce retries per hash length), line 150 (12 fallback hash length), line 161 (1000 safety break), line 169 (2000 hard stop). These control the collision-avoidance algorithm and should be documented constants.

WHAT "DONE" LOOKS LIKE: A single pub const DEFAULT_ID_PREFIX in util/id.rs, imported by config/mod.rs. MAX_REDIRECT_DEPTH const in config/mod.rs. SYNC_LOCK_FILENAME const in main.rs or a shared location. COMPLETION_TITLE_MAX_WIDTH const. HASH_DISPLAY_TRUNCATION_LEN const. All ID generation magic numbers named.

title: [MEDIUM] content_hash treats None and Some("") identically — field delimiter collision
description: In src/util/hash.rs:131, field_opt maps None to empty string via unwrap_or(""). This means field_opt(None) and field_opt(Some("")) produce identical hash input. While semantically equivalent for most fields, this creates a more subtle issue: adjacent None fields can collide with non-None fields due to the null-separator scheme. Example: title="A", description=None, design=Some("B") hashes the same sequence as title="A", description=Some(""), design=Some("B") — which is fine. BUT consider: title="A\x00", description=None — the null byte in title is replaced by space (line 123), but the field boundary null separator still exists. The real risk is that the null-separator scheme doesn't distinguish between (field="abc", next_field="") and (field="abc", next_field=None) which could matter if the schema evolves. Currently low-impact because None and empty string are treated as equivalent throughout the codebase. File: src/util/hash.rs:130-132. Test: proptest with None vs Some("") for each optional field.
close_reason: Not a bug — None and Some("") are semantically equivalent in this context. The null-separator scheme correctly prevents field boundary collisions.

title: config Command Implementation
description:
## Overview
Implement the `br config` command for viewing and modifying br configuration. Supports the layered configuration system (CLI > env > project > user > SQLite > defaults).

## CLI Interface
```
br config [SUBCOMMAND] [OPTIONS]

Subcommands:
  get <key>                 Get a config value
  set <key> <value>         Set a config value
  unset <key>               Remove a config value
  list                      List all config values
  edit                      Open config in editor
  path                      Show config file paths
  init                      Create default config file

Options:
  --global                  Use user-level config (~/.config/br/config.yaml)
  --project                 Use project-level config (.beads/config.yaml)
  --db                      Use SQLite-stored config
  --show-source             Show where each value comes from
  --json                    Output as JSON
```

## Technical Requirements

### Configuration Layering
Priority order (highest to lowest):
1. CLI flags (--prefix, etc.)
2. Environment variables (BR_PREFIX, etc.)
3. Project config (.beads/config.yaml)
4. User config (~/.config/br/config.yaml)
5. SQLite config table
6. Hard-coded defaults

```rust
pub struct ConfigResolver {
    cli_args: HashMap<String, String>,
    env_prefix: &str,
    project_config: Option<Config>,
    user_config: Option<Config>,
    db_config: HashMap<String, String>,
    defaults: HashMap<String, String>,
}

impl ConfigResolver {
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<ConfigValue> {
        // Check each layer in order
        if let Some(v) = self.cli_args.get(key) {
            return Some(ConfigValue { value: v.clone(), source: ConfigSource::Cli });
        }
        if let Some(v) = std::env::var(format!("BR_{}", key.to_uppercase())).ok() {
            return Some(ConfigValue { value: v, source: ConfigSource::Env });
        }
        // ... continue through layers
    }
    
    pub fn get_all_with_sources(&self) -> Vec<(String, ConfigValue)> {
        // Return all config keys with their effective values and sources
    }
}
```

### Config File Format (YAML)
```yaml
# .beads/config.yaml
prefix: bd                    # Issue ID prefix
default_priority: 2           # Default priority for new issues
default_type: task            # Default issue type
auto_flush: true              # Auto-export after changes
sync_on_init: true            # Import JSONL on init if newer
editor: ${EDITOR:-vim}        # Editor for edit commands

# Output preferences
color: auto                   # auto, always, never
format: human                 # human, json, robot

# Paths
database: .beads/bd.db        # SQLite database path
jsonl_dir: .beads             # JSONL export directory
```

### YAML-Only vs SQLite Keys
From the documentation:
- **YAML-only**: editor, color, format, paths (never stored in SQLite)
- **SQLite-capable**: prefix, default_priority, default_type, auto_flush

### Environment Variables
```
BR_PREFIX          - Issue ID prefix
BR_DEFAULT_PRIORITY - Default priority
BR_COLOR           - Color output (auto/always/never)
BR_FORMAT          - Output format
BR_DATABASE        - Database path
```

## Output Formats

### config list (human)
```
Configuration (merged from all sources):

Key               Value          Source
───────────────────────────────────────────
prefix            bd             project (.beads/config.yaml)
default_priority  2              default
default_type      task           default
auto_flush        true           user (~/.config/br/config.yaml)
color             auto           env (BR_COLOR)
editor            vim            default
```

### config list --json
```json
{
  "values": {
    "prefix": { "value": "bd", "source": "project" },
    "default_priority": { "value": "2", "source": "default" }
  },
  "paths": {
    "project": ".beads/config.yaml",
    "user": "/home/user/.config/br/config.yaml"
  }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] config get <key> returns effective value
- [ ] config set <key> <value> writes to appropriate config
- [ ] config unset <key> removes config value
- [ ] config list shows all values with sources
- [ ] --global flag targets user config
- [ ] --project flag targets project config
- [ ] --db flag targets SQLite config
- [ ] config path shows all config file locations
- [ ] config edit opens editor
- [ ] Environment variable override works
- [ ] Layering priority is correct

## Unit Tests
- Default values returned when no config
- Project config overrides default
- User config falls back when no project config
- Env vars override file config
- CLI args override everything
- YAML-only keys never read from SQLite
- set/get round-trip works
- unset removes value

## Dependencies
- SQLite Storage Layer (for db config)
- Model Types (Config struct)

## Rationale
Layered configuration allows users to set project-specific preferences while maintaining personal defaults. The config command makes this system transparent and debuggable.

title: Track: dep list should support sorting by priority instead of only by ID
description:
SUBTASK 7.3 (DEFERRED FEATURE): src/cli/commands/dep.rs:903 contains:
  "For now, let us sort by ID to be deterministic, or fetch details. Priority sorting would require fetching issues."

CURRENT BEHAVIOR: The dep list command sorts dependencies by ID string (lexicographic). This is deterministic but not useful for triage — a user running br dep list bd-X wants to see the highest-priority blockers first.

DESIRED BEHAVIOR: Add a --sort=priority flag (or make priority the default) that fetches the full issue for each dependency and sorts by priority descending.

IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATIONS:
- The current code avoids fetching issues for performance (dep list only queries the dependencies table)
- Priority sorting requires N additional get_issue() calls (one per dependency) which adds latency for issues with many deps
- Could batch-fetch with a single SQL query: SELECT * FROM issues WHERE id IN (dep1, dep2, ...) ORDER BY priority ASC
- For most issues, N < 10 deps, so the performance impact is negligible
- Could cache the results since the same issue might appear in multiple dep lists
- Consider making ID sort the default for --json (deterministic, machine-friendly) and priority sort the default for interactive/rich mode (human-friendly)

PRIORITY: P4/backlog because the current behavior is correct (deterministic, complete), just not optimally sorted for human use.
close_reason: Made human dep list output priority-aware while preserving JSON/TOON machine output order

title: doctor --repair reports a locked database as JSONL corruption
description:
When another process holds the SQLite database open, 'br doctor --repair --json' fails with:

    Configuration error: Repair import failed: Database error: unable to open database file: '<path>/.beads/beads.db'. The JSONL file may be corrupt. Try manually editing the JSONL to fix invalid records.

The hint is wrong and actively harmful. The JSONL is fine; the database could not be opened exclusively. Following the advice means hand-editing a healthy JSONL file, and an agent parsing the message would conclude the export is corrupt.

Reproduced by tests/e2e_workspace_commands.rs::e2e_doctor_repair_json_rebuilds_and_returns_single_payload, which held a raw Connection open across the repair (fixed separately in the test). The same condition occurs in real use whenever a second br process, an editor plugin, or an MCP 'br serve' session has the workspace open.

Fix: distinguish 'cannot open database' from 'import parse failure' on the repair path and emit a hint naming the real remedy (close other br processes / check .write.lock), rather than attributing it to JSONL corruption.
close_reason: Fixed. Variant-based classification replaces the residual bucket: FrankenError::CannotOpen/DatabaseLocked/LockFailed/Busy now yield 'the JSONL is not implicated' plus the real remedy (.write.lock, other br processes, br serve); JsonlParse/PrefixMismatch/ImportCollision keep pointing at the export; everything else reports without attributing a cause. --repair --dry-run no longer masquerades as a repair failure (outcome 'skipped', message verbatim). 5 new unit tests.

title: Benchmark baselines + regression thresholds
description:
Define baseline expectations and regression detection for benchmark runs.

## Scope
Establish performance baselines and automated regression detection for br commands.

### Baseline Metrics

**Per Command Group:**
- `list` operations: median time, p95 time, RSS peak
- `search` operations: median time, p95 time for various query complexities
- `create` operations: median time including JSONL flush
- `sync` operations: import/export time for various dataset sizes
- `ready`/`blocked` operations: time including dependency resolution

**Per Dataset Size:**
- Small (100 issues): baseline for quick feedback
- Medium (1,000 issues): typical project size
- Large (10,000 issues): stress testing
- XL (100,000 issues): scale limits

### Statistical Methodology

**Sampling:**
- Minimum 10 runs per measurement (configurable via BR_BENCH_RUNS)
- Warm-up run discarded before measurement
- Cold-start measured separately from warm-start

**Metrics:**
- Median (p50): primary metric for stability
- p95: tail latency for worst-case
- RSS peak: memory high-water mark
- RSS delta: memory growth during operation

**Outlier Handling:**
- Use IQR method: discard values outside [Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR]
- Report outlier count in summary

### Regression Detection

**Thresholds (configurable via env):**
- Time regression: >20% slower than baseline (BR_BENCH_TIME_THRESHOLD=0.20)
- Memory regression: >50% higher RSS than baseline (BR_BENCH_MEM_THRESHOLD=0.50)
- CI threshold: stricter 10% for time (BR_CI=1 mode)

**Comparison:**
- Compare against stored baseline.json
- Report: PASS (within threshold), WARN (5-20% regression), FAIL (>20% regression)
- Generate trend chart data for historical analysis

### Baseline Storage

**Format:**
```json
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "generated_at": "2026-01-20T12:00:00Z",
  "br_version": "0.9.5",
  "br_commit": "abc1234",
  "baselines": {
    "list_small": {"p50_ms": 45, "p95_ms": 62, "rss_mb": 12},
    "list_medium": {"p50_ms": 120, "p95_ms": 180, "rss_mb": 45},
    ...
  }
}
```

**Location:**
- benchmarks/baseline.json (committed to repo)
- Update via: `cargo bench --features baseline-update`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Baseline metrics established for all command groups
- [ ] Regression detection flags >20% time increase
- [ ] Summary table shows pass/warn/fail status per metric
- [ ] CI mode uses stricter thresholds
- [ ] Historical trend data exportable

## Test Coverage (tests/bench_baselines.rs)
- baseline_generation: verify baseline.json created with correct schema
- regression_detection_pass: verify no alert when within threshold
- regression_detection_warn: verify warning at 10-20% regression
- regression_detection_fail: verify failure at >20% regression
- threshold_override: verify BR_BENCH_*_THRESHOLD env vars work
- ci_mode_thresholds: verify stricter thresholds when BR_CI=1
- outlier_filtering: verify IQR outlier removal

## Output Format
```
Benchmark Results (br v0.9.5 @ abc1234)
┌─────────────────┬──────────┬──────────┬─────────┬────────┐
│ Command         │ p50 (ms) │ p95 (ms) │ RSS (MB)│ Status │
├─────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┼─────────┼────────┤
│ list (small)    │ 42       │ 58       │ 11      │ ✓ PASS │
│ list (medium)   │ 135 (+12%)│ 195     │ 48      │ ⚠ WARN │
│ list (large)    │ 890 (+25%)│ 1200    │ 180     │ ✗ FAIL │
└─────────────────┴──────────┴──────────┴─────────┴────────┘
```

## Logging Requirements
- [BENCH] Running list (medium) - run 1/10
- [BENCH] Run 1: 132ms, RSS 45MB
- [BENCH] Outlier detected: 892ms (>IQR, discarded)
- [BASELINE] list (medium): p50=120ms → 135ms (+12.5%) ⚠ WARN

title: Refresh insta snapshot goldens after --slug feature (PR #283)
description:
## Summary

About 20 insta snapshot golden tests in `tests/snapshots.rs` (and the related `agent_baseline_snapshots_match_current_binary` in `e2e_schema`) fail locally because the CLI changed without their `.snap` files being refreshed. The biggest known cause: commit `5c0af3d4 feat(create): --slug for human-readable issue IDs (#283)` (2026-05-07) added the `--slug` flag without `cargo insta review`. **That commit has no closed bead in `.beads/issues.jsonl`** — feature-shipped-without-bead-at-all, in addition to the snapshot drift.

## Affected snapshot tests (verified locally 2026-05-09)

```
snapshots::cli_output::snapshot_help_output
snapshots::cli_output::snapshot_create_help
snapshots::cli_output::snapshot_version_output
snapshots::error_messages::snapshot_error_invalid_priority
snapshots::error_messages::snapshot_error_issue_not_found
snapshots::error_messages::snapshot_error_self_dependency
snapshots::error_messages::snapshot_error_dependency_cycle
snapshots::error_messages::snapshot_error_update_closed_issue
snapshots::history_diff_output::history_diff_golden_json_summary_v0_1_0_to_v0_1_1
snapshots::json_output::representative_json_golden_list_output
snapshots::json_output::representative_json_golden_show_output
snapshots::json_output::snapshot_create_json
snapshots::json_output::snapshot_list_json
snapshots::json_output::snapshot_search_json
snapshots::json_output::snapshot_show_json
snapshots::json_output::snapshot_list_with_filters_json
snapshots::json_output::snapshot_show_multiple_ids_json
snapshots::json_output::snapshot_list_priority_ordering_json
snapshots::jsonl_format::snapshot_jsonl_export
e2e_schema::agent_baseline_snapshots_match_current_binary
```

## Why this matters beyond just "run insta review"

This is exactly the completion theater the audit was looking for: a feature shipped, the test suite went red on its baselines, and somebody (a) kept committing past it or (b) CI does not enforce snapshot freshness. **A blind `cargo insta accept`** would re-bake the regression into goldens *if* any of the 20 deltas captures a bug rather than the intended `--slug` addition. Each delta needs human review.

## Investigation steps

1. **Reproduce locally**:
   ```bash
   RCH_DISABLED=1 cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test snapshots --test e2e_schema 2>&1 | tee /tmp/l6xl-repro.log
   ```

title: EPIC: Installation & Distribution Automation
description:
# Installation & Distribution Automation

## Background & Rationale

Based on research of mature Rust/Go CLI tools (xf, cass, beads_viewer) and 2025-2026 distribution best practices, br needs a professional-grade installation and update system that makes adoption frictionless and secure.

### Why This Matters
- One-liner installation is the gold standard for CLI tool adoption
- Users expect tools to auto-update (or easily update) themselves
- Multi-platform support (Linux, macOS, Windows; x86_64, ARM64) is table stakes
- Security requires checksum verification and signed releases
- AI coding agents benefit from automated tool management

## Goals
Deliver a complete distribution system that enables users to install br with a single command, receive automatic updates, and trust the integrity of downloaded binaries.

## Deliverables

### 1. Multi-Platform Installer Script
- Platform detection (Linux/macOS/Windows, amd64/arm64)
- Download from GitHub Releases with checksum verification
- Fallback to source build if binary unavailable
- Idempotent installation (safe to re-run)
- Lock mechanism to prevent concurrent installs
- Resume capability for interrupted downloads
- PATH modification with shell detection

### 2. Self-Update Command
- `br update` - Check for and install updates
- `br update --check` - Check only, don't install
- `br update --force` - Force reinstall current version
- Use `self_update` or `patchify` crate
- Ed25519 signature verification
- SHA256 hash verification of downloaded files
- Streaming downloads for large files

### 3. Release Automation
- GitHub Actions workflow for multi-platform builds
- Automatic checksum generation
- Release asset naming convention
- Changelog generation from closed issues

### 4. Package Manager Distribution
- Homebrew tap: `brew install dicklesworthstone/tap/br`
- Scoop bucket for Windows users
- AUR package for Arch Linux
- crates.io publishing for Rust users

### 5. Version Management
- Semantic versioning (SemVer)
- `br version` shows build info, git commit, build date
- `br version --check` shows if update available

## Acceptance Criteria
- Single-command installation on all supported platforms
- `br update` successfully updates the binary in-place
- All downloads verified with checksums
- Installation is fully idempotent
- Works behind corporate proxies (HTTPS_PROXY support)

## Technical Approach

### Installer Script Pattern
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../install.sh | bash
# OR
curl -fsSL https://br.tools/install | bash
```

### Self-Update with self_update crate
```toml
[dependencies]
self_update = { version = "0.27", features = ["rustls"], default-features = false }
```

### Release Profile (already in place)
```toml
[profile.release]
opt-level = "z"     # Size optimization
lto = true           # Link-time optimization
codegen-units = 1    # Single codegen unit
panic = "abort"      # No unwinding
strip = true         # Remove symbols
```

## Security Considerations
- Ed25519 signatures for release files
- SHA256 checksums in separate .sha256 files
- HTTPS-only downloads (rustls, no OpenSSL)
- Verify before replace (atomic update)

## References
- self_update crate: https://github.com/jaemk/self_update
- patchify crate: https://github.com/danwilliams/patchify
- trust project: CI release builds
- ACFS manifest pattern for tool distribution

## Dependencies
- CI/CD Pipeline (beads_rust-na7)
- version Command (beads_rust-k8p) - completed

title: [test-debt] Audit and migrate ID-pinning anti-patterns across tests/ tree
description:
## Summary

The `storage_ready::ready_sort_policy_*` failures (in `beads_rust-jsgu`) are the visible tip of a broader anti-pattern: tests asserting equality on generated content-hash IDs (`test-XXXXXXXX`, `tmpXXXXXX-XXX`, `bd-XXX`, `br-XXX`) instead of asserting on the *invariants* the IDs are meant to embody (ordering, presence, uniqueness, round-trip equality).

This bead audits the entire `tests/` tree for ID-pinning anti-patterns and migrates them to invariant-based assertions, using the helper module added in `beads_rust-jsgu`.

## Investigation steps

1. **Inventory likely ID-pinning sites**:
   ```bash
   cd /data/projects/beads_rust
   rg --no-heading -tn 'assert_eq!\([^,]*,\s*"(test|tmp|br|bd|proj)-[a-zA-Z0-9]{4,}"' tests/ \
     | tee /tmp/id-pinning-candidates.txt
   wc -l /tmp/id-pinning-candidates.txt
   ```
2. **Triage each match** into:
   - **True ID-pinning** (assertion of generated content-hash equality) — must migrate
   - **Fixture round-trip** (creating an issue with explicit ID, then asserting `br show <id>` returns the same ID) — KEEP, this is invariant-based
   - **Hardcoded prefix expectation** (intentional cross-tool compatibility test) — KEEP, document with a comment

3. **Look at the symmetric `assert_ne!` form** as well:
   ```bash
   rg --no-heading -tn 'assert_ne!\([^,]*,\s*"(test|tmp|br|bd|proj)-[a-zA-Z0-9]{4,}"' tests/
   ```

4. **Check property tests** for similar patterns — `tests/proptest_*.rs` may have shrunk-fixture pinning.

## Plan

### Step 1: Inventory + triage table

Produce `docs/audit_id_pinning_2026_05_09.md` with one row per match:
`file:line | excerpt | category | proposed action`

This becomes the worklist.

### Step 2: Migrate

For each "true ID-pinning" hit, rewrite using the helper module from `beads_rust-jsgu` (`tests/common/ordering.rs`) — extending it with new helpers as needed:

- `assert_contains_issue_with_title(issues, expected_title)`
- `assert_round_trip_id(storage, original_id)` (fixture round-trip)
- `assert_ordered_by_priority(issues)`
- `assert_no_duplicate_ids(issues)`

### Step 3: Lint pattern (sibling bead `[lint]`)

A grep / clippy pattern that fails CI on new ID-pinning hits is its own bead — see linked sibling.

## Required tests

### Migrations
- [ ] Every "true ID-pinning" hit in the inventory is migrated to invariant-based assertion
- [ ] Every "fixture round-trip" hit gets a leading `// invariant: round-trip; not ID-pinning` comment so future audits don't flag it
- [ ] Every "hardcoded prefix expectation" hit gets a leading `// invariant: cross-tool compatibility; not ID-pinning` comment

### NEW helper tests (extend `tests/common/ordering.rs::tests`)

- [ ] **NEW** `assert_contains_issue_with_title_panics_with_full_list_on_no_match`
- [ ] **NEW** `assert_round_trip_id_succeeds_after_create`
- [ ] **NEW** `assert_no_duplicate_ids_passes_on_unique_set`

### Regression check
- [ ] After migrations: `cargo test --release --no-fail-fast` exits 0
- [ ] 50× flake check on the migrated tests passes 50/50
- [ ] `rg --no-heading -tn 'assert_eq!\([^,]*,\s*"(test|tmp|br|bd|proj)-[a-zA-Z0-9]{4,}"' tests/ | wc -l` → 0 (or only commented intentional hits)

## Logging requirements

- Helper assertions panic with rich context naming the inputs and the violated invariant.
- Audit results documented in `docs/audit_id_pinning_2026_05_09.md` (one row per migrated test).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Inventory document `docs/audit_id_pinning_2026_05_09.md` exists and is committed
- [ ] All "true ID-pinning" tests migrated (status: green)
- [ ] All "fixture round-trip" and "intentional" hits annotated with comments
- [ ] No new test failures introduced

## Verification command

RCH_DISABLED=1 cargo test --release --no-fail-fast 2>&1 | tee /tmp/idpin-verify.log
echo "exit: $?"
rg --no-heading -tn 'assert_eq!\([^,]*,\s*"(test|tmp|br|bd|proj)-[a-zA-Z0-9]{4,}"' tests/ | wc -l

title: Program: CI/release workflow supply-chain hardening and proof
description:
Idea-wizard result after the live queue went dry on 2026-05-08. Phase 1 grounding: AGENTS.md and README.md were reread; br/bv showed no ready/open/in_progress work; Agent Mail was green and no ack-required messages were pending. Recent closed work already covers swarm-scale performance, read-only coordination observability, stale-claim diagnosis, MCP coordination status, recovery/doctor hardening, crash/contention labs, and many perf evidence loops. Search did not find an existing workflow action pinning or CI supply-chain governance bead.

Phase 2 broad 30 ideas considered:
1. First-class GitHub Actions pin manifest plus verifier.
2. Release workflow shell-fragment regression harness.
3. Scheduled workflow dependency drift report for pinned SHAs.
4. Notify-ACFS dry-run contract tests.

6. Enforced actionlint/yq gate for workflow PRs.
7. Provenance/SLSA release preflight checklist with machine checks.
8. Reusable checksum/signature shell helper tests.

11. Artifact upload/download path consistency tests.
12. Release notes generator golden fixtures.
13. Installer curl-pipe smoke harness in CI.
14. Cross-target release matrix verifier.
15. GitHub token/secrets least-privilege audit.
16. Workflow concurrency/cancel behavior tests.
17. Rust toolchain pin freshness report.
18. External action availability fallback notes.
19. SBOM generation failure-mode tests.
20. Package-manifest update workflow dry-run tests.
21. Branch mirror policy sentinel.
22. Release asset naming schema verifier.
23. Markdown badge/link freshness check.
24. Docs-to-workflow command parity check.
25. Security audit workflow severity policy cleanup.
26. CI runtime budget dashboard.
27. Cache-key invalidation tests.
28. Nightly toolchain drift detector.
29. End-to-end release rehearsal checklist.
30. Emergency rollback playbook for bad workflow pin.

Phase 2 top 5 selected, in order:
1. Workflow action pin manifest and verifier. This is the highest-leverage follow-up because the repo now uses immutable action SHAs, but there is no machine-readable inventory proving which tag each SHA came from or whether a future edit reintroduces a mutable ref.
2. Release workflow shell-fragment regression harness. actionlint caught real shell reliability hazards in release/notification scripts. A focused harness would prevent fragile release notes/checksum code from regressing without running a real release.
3. Scheduled or manual action update audit. Immutable pins are safer but can go stale. A report-only command/workflow should show candidate tag updates without mutating files automatically.
4. Notify-ACFS dry-run contract coverage. The installer notification workflow is production-adjacent and token-gated; it should have fixture-style proof that checksum comparison, dry_run, missing-token, and summary behavior work.
5. CI/release supply-chain maintenance policy. Future agents need explicit rules for why action SHAs are pinned, how to update them, which commands verify them, and how to keep main mirrored.

Phase 3 next 10 retained as future optional refinements: enforced actionlint/yq gate, provenance preflight checklist, checksum/signature helper tests, permission minimization audit, immutable-pin update guidance, artifact path consistency, release notes golden fixtures, installer curl-pipe smoke harness, cross-target release matrix verifier, and token/secrets least-privilege audit.

Goal: make CI/release workflow edits as evidence-backed and non-surprising as Rust code edits. title: Create AGENTS.md generation script for VPS root
description:
## Context
Part of agentic_coding_flywheel_setup #68 fix. Create a script that generates /AGENTS.md.

## Why a Script (Not Static File)
- Tools evolve, documentation should stay current
- Can pull version info dynamically
- Enables weekly automated updates
- Single source of truth for generation logic

## Script Design

### Location
- agentic_coding_flywheel_setup/scripts/generate-root-agents-md.sh
- Or: /usr/local/bin/flywheel-update-agents-md

### Script Logic
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Generate /AGENTS.md for flywheel VPS

OUTPUT="/AGENTS.md"
TIMESTAMP=$(date -Iseconds)

cat > "$OUTPUT" << 'HEADER'
# Flywheel VPS - Agent Guidelines
> Auto-generated: $TIMESTAMP
> Regenerate: flywheel-update-agents-md

HEADER

# Add tool documentation
for tool in ru br bv ntm; do
  echo "## $tool"
  $tool --help 2>/dev/null | head -50
  echo ""
done

# Add static workflow content from template
cat /path/to/workflows-template.md >> "$OUTPUT"
```

### Template Content
Static sections that don't change often:
- Flywheel loop explanation
- Common workflows
- Troubleshooting tips
- Resource links

### Permissions
- Script runs as root or with sudo
- Output file readable by all users
- /AGENTS.md owned by root:root, mode 644

## Testing
1. Run script manually
2. Verify /AGENTS.md created
3. Verify content is accurate
4. Test with different tool versions

## Deliverable
- Working generation script
- Template for static content
- Installation instructions

title: Fix blocked_issues_cache unique constraint when claiming ready issues
description:
While working beads_rust-gzd1 on 2026-03-25, `br update beads_rust-gzd1 --status in_progress --json` failed even though the issue was ready. The command returned DATABASE_ERROR: `UNIQUE constraint failed: blocked_issues_cache.issue_id`.

Observed context:
- beads_rust-9ox0 had just been closed successfully
- `br ready --json` showed beads_rust-gzd1 as actionable
- `br blocked --json` did not list it as blocked
- a plain `br update ... --status in_progress` still failed with the uniqueness violation

This suggests blocked cache maintenance can insert duplicate rows during claim/update flows. Repro may involve closing a dependency and then immediately claiming a newly-unblocked dependent.

title: [doctor] Add audit.suspect_close_reasons check to flag forced-cycle-close pattern
description:
## Summary

Add a `br doctor` check (and optionally a `br lint` rule) that flags closed beads with audit-suspect `close_reason` text patterns like "Forced close due to cycle" / "due to dependency cycle". This is the preventive layer for `beads_rust-30ci` — once we triage the existing 5, this guardrail prevents the pattern from recurring silently.

**Blocked by `beads_rust-30ci`** because the historical-triage escape-hatch label must be defined first.

## Approach

Add a new check to `src/cli/commands/doctor.rs`.

### Check name (proposed): `audit.suspect_close_reasons`

### Severity: `warn` (not `fail`) — these aren't broken DBs, just audit-suspect closures.

### Default detection patterns (regex, case-insensitive):

```
- forced.*close.*cycle
- due to.*dep.*cycle
- temporarily closed
- wip close
- to be ([rR]e)?opened
- closing for now
```

### Default-allowlist (skip patterns that ARE legitimate)

To avoid false positives, the check ships with an allowlist of close_reason fragments that should NEVER be flagged:

```
- auto-closed by doctor      # legitimate doctor remediation
- closed by epic close-eligible   # br epic close-eligible flow
- closed via br epic close   # epic-driven closure
- merged into                # merged-into-other-bead pattern
- superseded by              # supersedes flow
```

These are case-insensitive substring matches. Operator can override via config.

### Output shape

```json
{
  "name": "audit.suspect_close_reasons",
  "status": "warn",
  "message": "5 closed beads have audit-suspect close_reason text",
  "details": {
    "patterns_used": ["forced.*close.*cycle", ...],
    "allowlist_used": ["auto-closed by doctor", ...],
    "matches": [
      {
        "bead_id": "beads_rust-aeb",
        "matched_pattern": "forced.*close.*cycle",
        "close_reason": "Implemented list command. Forced close due to cycle.",
        "has_historical_label": false
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Exception escape hatch (defined by sibling 30ci)

Beads carrying the label `audit-historical-cycle-close-<YYYY>-<MM>-<DD>` (or `audit-suspect-allowed`) are excluded from the check — this lets `beads_rust-30ci`'s "Accept as historical" decision survive the doctor gate.

### Configurable patterns (config.yaml)

Make the regex list AND allowlist configurable via `~/.config/beads/config.yaml` or `.beads/config.yaml` under a new key:

```yaml
doctor:
  suspect_close_reason_patterns:
    - "(?i)forced.*close.*cycle"
    - "(?i)due to.*dep.*cycle"
  suspect_close_reason_allowlist:
    - "auto-closed by doctor"
    - "closed by epic close-eligible"
    - "merged into"
  suspect_close_reason_excluded_labels:
    - "audit-historical-cycle-close-2026-05-09"
    - "audit-suspect-allowed"
```

## Schema integration

The new check shape MUST be reflected in the JSON Schema emitted by `br schema all`. Specifically:

- [ ] Update `src/cli/commands/schema.rs` (or wherever the schema generator lives) to include the new check in the `DoctorEnvelope` schema definition
- [ ] `br schema all --format json | jq '.schemas.DoctorCheck.properties.name.enum'` must include `"audit.suspect_close_reasons"`
- [ ] `br schema all --format toon` must reflect the new check in TOON output too

## MCP integration

If the `mcp` feature is enabled, the resource `beads://graph/health` (which exposes doctor results) must include the new check. No additional code change should be needed if doctor's JSON envelope is the source of truth, but verify.

## Plan

### Step 1: Add the check
- New function in `src/cli/commands/doctor.rs`: `fn check_suspect_close_reasons(storage: &dyn Storage, config: &DoctorConfig) -> CheckResult`
- Wire into the existing check sequence
- Add to the `--json` envelope

### Step 2: Configurable patterns + allowlist
- Add new keys to the config schema under `doctor:`
- Default patterns + default allowlist as constants in source (so an empty config still produces sensible behavior)
- Per-project override merges with defaults (don't replace)

### Step 3: Update JSON schema generator + TOON
- Ensure `br schema all` reflects the new check

### Step 4: Tests

Cover the obvious cases.

## Required tests

### Unit tests (in `src/cli/commands/doctor.rs::tests`)
- [ ] **NEW** `check_suspect_close_reasons_finds_matching_bead`
- [ ] **NEW** `check_suspect_close_reasons_skips_beads_with_historical_label`
- [ ] **NEW** `check_suspect_close_reasons_returns_ok_when_no_matches`
- [ ] **NEW** `check_suspect_close_reasons_respects_configurable_patterns_from_config`
- [ ] **NEW** `check_suspect_close_reasons_skips_default_allowlist` — beads closed via `br epic close-eligible` should not flag
- [ ] **NEW** `check_suspect_close_reasons_user_allowlist_merges_with_default` — user adds custom allowlist entry; both default and custom apply
- [ ] **NEW** `check_suspect_close_reasons_emits_match_pattern_in_envelope` — `matched_pattern` field is populated for each hit

### E2E (in `tests/e2e_audit.rs` if it exists, else new)
- [ ] **NEW** `e2e_doctor_warns_on_suspect_close_reason` — creates a bead, closes with offending reason, runs `br doctor --json`, asserts the warn shows up
- [ ] **NEW** `e2e_doctor_silent_when_only_historical_labels` — same, but with the historical label; warn must not fire
- [ ] **NEW** `e2e_doctor_silent_when_close_reason_in_allowlist` — same, but close_reason matches default allowlist
- [ ] **NEW** `e2e_doctor_check_present_in_schema_output` — `br schema all --format json | jq` confirms the check is documented

### Shell harness
- [ ] **NEW** `tests/e2e_scripts/doctor_suspect_close_reasons.sh` — drives full lifecycle including the historical-label escape hatch and the allowlist; emits structured PASS/FAIL log

### Schema regression
- [ ] **NEW** `tests/conformance_schema.rs` extension: snapshot `br schema all --format json | jq '.schemas.DoctorEnvelope'` to ensure backward-compatible additive changes only.

## Logging requirements

- The doctor check emits `tracing::info!` `doctor_check_run` events with `name`, `status`, `match_count`, `patterns_used_count`, `allowlist_size`.
- `--json` output includes the full match list for programmatic remediation.
- Each match in the envelope MUST cite the matched pattern so operators can adjust patterns without re-reading source.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New `check_suspect_close_reasons` function exists, registered in the doctor sequence
- [ ] All 7 new unit tests pass
- [ ] All 4 new e2e tests pass
- [ ] New shell harness exits 0 with PASS summary
- [ ] Configurable patterns AND allowlist in `config.yaml` work (default + override)
- [ ] `br doctor --json` envelope includes the new check
- [ ] `br schema all --format json` reflects the new check shape
- [ ] `br schema all --format toon` reflects the new check shape too (TOON parity)
- [ ] If `mcp` feature on: `beads://graph/health` MCP resource includes the check
- [ ] `docs/DOCTOR_CHECKS.md` (new file or section) documents the check
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` clean

## Verification command

```bash
cd /data/projects/beads_rust
RCH_DISABLED=1 cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test e2e_audit --test conformance_schema -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee /tmp/m3mi-verify.log
echo "exit: $?"
bash tests/e2e_scripts/doctor_suspect_close_reasons.sh
br doctor --json | jq '.checks[] | select(.name == "audit.suspect_close_reasons")'
br schema all --format json | jq '.schemas.DoctorEnvelope' >/dev/null && echo "schema present" || echo "schema MISSING"
```

## Source

beads_compliance_audit pass `2026-05-09T01-00-44Z`. Parent EPIC: `beads_rust-ebzi`. **Blocked by `beads_rust-30ci`** (historical-triage label must be defined first). Sibling: `beads_rust-30ci` (the retroactive-triage bead).

Clippy + fmt clean. Configurable-patterns + schema-doc-regression deferred (additive enhancements).

title: br graph traverses dependents where bd traverses dependencies
description:
## Symptom

'br graph <id>' walks the dependency graph in the opposite direction to 'bd graph <id>'. Verified by hand against a real classic bd v0.46.0 on 2026-07-25.

Reproduction (br 0.2.19):

    br init --prefix bd
    A=$(br create 'Issue A' --json | jq -r .id)   # bd-t11
    B=$(br create 'Issue B' --json | jq -r .id)   # bd-cgb
    br dep add $A $B      # A depends on B; prints 'Added dependency: bd-t11 -> bd-cgb (blocks)'
    br dep list $A --json  # [{issue_id: bd-t11, depends_on_id: bd-cgb, type: blocks}]

    br graph $A --json
    {"root":"bd-t11","nodes":[{"id":"bd-t11",...}],"edges":[],"count":1}

    br graph $B --json
    {"root":"bd-cgb","nodes":[{"id":"bd-cgb",...},{"id":"bd-t11",...,"depth":1}],"edges":[["bd-t11","bd-cgb"]],"count":2}

So asking for the graph of the issue that HAS a dependency shows nothing, while asking for the graph of its blocker shows the edge. br traverses dependents (who is blocked by the root); bd traverses dependencies (what the root is blocked by).

## Why it matters beyond parity

Independent of bd, this is surprising on its own terms. README documents 'graph | Visualize dependency graph | br graph br-abc123'. A user who runs 'br graph <id>' on an issue they cannot start expects to see what is blocking it. Today they get a single node and no edges.

## Conformance impact

Three tests assert bd's direction and are now #[ignore]d pointing at this issue: conformance_graph_simple_dep, conformance_graph_complex_deps, conformance_graph_all_flag (tests/conformance.rs). They were failing in the first real br-bd conformance run (beads_rust-ecr6).

## Decision needed

Either (a) br graph should traverse dependencies to match bd and user expectation, (b) it should show both directions, or (c) the current behavior is deliberate and the three conformance tests should stay ignored permanently with that rationale recorded. This is a user-visible behavior change, so it needs the owner's call rather than a silent flip.
close_reason: Implemented br graph --dependencies. The default dependents walk is unchanged and stays the default -- it is deliberate, and graph.rs documents it -- but one command now covers both directions instead of sending users to br dep tree. Added SqliteStorage::get_blocking_dependencies_for_issue_ids as the exact inverse of the dependents query (including the parent-child special case), a GraphDirection enum threaded through collect_single_graph/cache_graph_dependents, and direction-aware human output ('Dependencies of X by depth', 'No dependencies for X', and the rich panel's neighbour noun). Edges keep their canonical (dependent, dependency) orientation in both directions; depth is computed from reversed edges in the dependencies direction so it still means 'hops from the root' (verified 0,1,2 both ways). --dependencies conflicts_with --all so the semantics stay unambiguous. Discoverability fixed too: help, the ISSUE arg description, the GraphArgs doc comment and the README all state the direction. Tests: two storage tests asserting the inverse relation, two graph tests covering the walk and the flag mapping; graph:: 33/33, lib 2478/0, storage_deps 193/0.

comments.author: CoralLantern
comments.text:
Investigated: the direction is DELIBERATE, not a bug. src/cli/commands/graph.rs:3-5 says so at the top of the module:

  //! Visualizes dependency graphs with focus on reverse dependencies (dependents).
  //! - 'br graph <issue-id>': Show all dependents of an issue (what depends on it)

So 'br graph <id>' deliberately answers 'what does closing this unblock?', which is the triage question, and 'br dep tree <id>' covers the other direction. The parity gap against bd is real but is an intentional divergence in the same family as the ~20 already documented in tests/conformance.rs.

The genuine defect was DISCOVERABILITY, and that is what I fixed rather than flipping semantics:
- 'br graph --help' said 'Visualize dependency graph', which implies both directions. Now: 'Visualize the dependents graph: what an issue unblocks'.
- The ISSUE arg said 'Issue ID (root of graph)'. Now 'root of the dependents graph', with a GraphArgs doc comment spelling out that a blocked leaf reports no dependents and pointing at 'br dep tree' / 'br show'.
- README's command table said 'Visualize dependency graph'. Now 'Show what an issue unblocks (its dependents)'.
- The three conformance #[ignore] reasons now read 'br graph shows dependents by design; bd shows dependencies' instead of framing it as an unsettled question.

Remaining OPTIONAL enhancement, your call, and the only part I did not do because it is a feature rather than a fix: add a direction flag (e.g. 'br graph <id> --dependencies' or '--reverse') so one command covers both walks. Today a user who wants 'what is blocking this?' must switch to 'br dep tree'. If you want that flag, this bead is the place for it; otherwise it can close as documented-by-design.

title: Create multi-platform installer script
description:
# Multi-Platform Installer Script

## Purpose
Enable one-liner installation of br on Linux, macOS, and Windows with automatic platform detection, checksum verification, and idempotent behavior.

## Technical Requirements

### Script Features
- Platform detection (Linux/macOS/Windows)
- Architecture detection (x86_64/arm64)
- Download from GitHub Releases
- SHA256 checksum verification
- Fallback to source build if binary unavailable
- Idempotent (safe to re-run)
- Lock mechanism for concurrent protection
- Resume capability for interrupted downloads
- PATH modification with shell detection
- Proxy support (HTTPS_PROXY)

### Installation Methods
```bash
# Primary: curl
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/main/install.sh | bash

# Alternative: wget
wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust/main/install.sh | bash

# With options
curl -fsSL .../install.sh | bash -s -- --prefix=~/.local --no-modify-path
```

### Script Structure
```bash
#\!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Configuration
REPO="Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust"
BINARY_NAME="br"
INSTALL_DIR="${HOME}/.local/bin"

# Functions
detect_platform()     # linux_amd64, darwin_arm64, etc.
detect_shell()        # bash, zsh, fish
download_release()    # curl with retry
verify_checksum()     # sha256sum verification
install_binary()      # atomic install
modify_path()         # idempotent PATH update
build_from_source()   # fallback with Rust install

# Main
main() {
    parse_args "$@"
    acquire_lock
    trap cleanup EXIT
    
    PLATFORM="$(detect_platform)"
    
    if \! download_release "$PLATFORM"; then
        warn "Binary not available, building from source..."
        build_from_source
    fi
    
    verify_checksum
    install_binary
    [[ "$MODIFY_PATH" == "true" ]] \u0026\u0026 modify_path
    
    echo "✓ br installed successfully\!"
    echo "  Run 'br --help' to get started."
}
```

### Checksum Verification
```bash
verify_checksum() {
    local expected="$(curl -fsSL "${RELEASE_URL}.sha256")"
    local actual="$(sha256sum "$DOWNLOAD_PATH" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
    
    if [[ "$expected" \!= "$actual" ]]; then
        error "Checksum mismatch\! Expected: $expected, Got: $actual"
        exit 1
    fi
}
```

### Idempotency Patterns
- mkdir -p (creates if not exists)
- Check before PATH modify (grep for existing entry)
- Lock file with stale detection
- Atomic moves (mv, not cp)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Works on Ubuntu 22.04+, macOS 13+, Windows 11 (WSL)
- [ ] Detects x86_64 and arm64 architectures
- [ ] Verifies checksums before install
- [ ] Falls back to source build gracefully
- [ ] Idempotent (multiple runs don't break)
- [ ] Modifies PATH correctly for bash/zsh/fish
- [ ] Works behind HTTPS_PROXY
- [ ] Clear error messages on failure

## Files to Create
- `install.sh` - Main installer script
- `scripts/build-release.sh` - Build script for releases
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` - Release automation

## References
- ACFS install.sh patterns
- self_update crate documentation
- Homebrew installer conventions

title: [concurrency] e2e_read_command_witness_refresh_waits_for_write_lock fails - diagnose and harden
description:
`tests/e2e_concurrency.rs::e2e_read_command_witness_refresh_waits_for_write_lock` fails locally. This test exercises the read-path "witness refresh" semantics: a read command (e.g., `br list`, `br show`) that opens the database while a write is in progress must wait for the writer to release `.write.lock` before its witness refresh can succeed.

## Reproduction (deterministic seed)

```bash
cd /data/projects/beads_rust
PROPTEST_CASES=200 BCV_CONCURRENCY_SEED=42 RUST_LOG=trace RCH_DISABLED=1 \
  cargo test --release --no-fail-fast --test e2e_concurrency \
  -- --nocapture e2e_read_command_witness_refresh_waits_for_write_lock 2>&1 | tee /tmp/mjmk-repro.log
```

Concurrency tests are inherently nondeterministic. The fix MUST add a seed-driven mode (`BCV_CONCURRENCY_SEED` env var) so that any flaking observation can be reproduced byte-for-byte across machines.

## Hypothesis (ranked)

1. **Lock-acquisition timeout regression** — recent work (`beads_rust-kw8p` "Blocking .write.lock acquisition has no timeout or holder diagnostics") may have changed the wait semantics, leaving readers with a tighter timeout than writers' commit window.
2. **Witness refresh state machine drift** — the read-side observation that the write completed may now race with the writer's commit, allowing the read to proceed against a stale view.
3. **Platform-specific lock semantics** — `.write.lock` may use `flock` on Linux and `fcntl` (or LockFileEx on Windows) with subtly different semantics; recent changes may have only been tested on one.
4. **Filesystem mtime granularity** — if witness uses mtime to detect writes, ext4's nanosecond resolution differs from APFS / NTFS; could mask races on some platforms.

The sibling P0 sync-safety bead (`yyxo`) and this one may share root cause if a recent storage/sync refactor altered both paths. **`yyxo` blocks this bead** — fix sync allowlist first to keep this work on a stable foundation.

## Investigation steps (must do all)

1. **Identify the assertion that fails** — read `tests/e2e_concurrency.rs` source. Note the expected ordering: read must observe the write only after `.write.lock` is released.
2. **Run with `RUST_LOG=trace`** and capture all `storage::sqlite`, `storage::lock`, `sync::witness` log lines. Save to artifact.
3. **Run the test 50 times deterministically** to characterize flakiness:
   ```bash
   for seed in {1..50}; do
     BCV_CONCURRENCY_SEED=$seed RCH_DISABLED=1 \
       cargo test --release --test e2e_concurrency -q \
       -- e2e_read_command_witness_refresh_waits_for_write_lock 2>&1 \
       | tail -1 | grep -oE 'ok|FAILED' || echo NORUN
   done | sort | uniq -c
   ```
4. **Compare exit profiles across platforms** — run on Linux (current); if `mmini` (macOS arm64) or `wlap` (Windows x86_64) build hosts are accessible (see release-process.md), capture the same 50-run histogram on each. Document deltas.
5. **Inspect history of `src/storage/sqlite.rs` and `src/sync/`** for any change to write-lock acquisition / release order / witness refresh.
6. **(Optional but recommended) Run with `loom` or `shuttle`** for systematic concurrency exploration — these tools randomize thread interleavings and can find races deterministic stress-testing misses. See https://github.com/tokio-rs/loom.

## Fix path

Once root cause identified, the fix likely lives in `src/storage/sqlite.rs` (lock acquisition) or in the read-path witness logic. The test itself should NOT be relaxed — concurrency invariants are load-bearing.

## Required tests

### Unit tests (in `src/storage/sqlite.rs::tests`)
- [ ] **NEW** `write_lock_release_then_acquire_round_trips` — basic acquire→release→acquire
- [ ] **NEW** `write_lock_acquire_with_holder_diagnostics_after_timeout` — verify `kw8p` diagnostics
- [ ] **NEW** `read_command_witness_refresh_after_write_observes_new_state` — non-flaky version of the existing test using direct API calls instead of CLI subprocess
- [ ] **NEW** `write_lock_holder_pid_persists_across_reads` — confirms lock metadata isn't volatile

### Property test (new file: `tests/proptest_concurrency.rs`)
- [ ] **NEW** Property: any sequence of N writers + M readers produces a final state where every read observed at most one writer's committed state, never partial. Use `proptest!` with `WORKERS in 2..8usize` and `OPS in 10..100usize`. Seed-driven via `PROPTEST_CASES` and a fixed `Config::with_source_file_seed`.
- [ ] **NEW** Property: with N concurrent readers and 1 writer, exactly one read must transition `db_mtime_observed_pre < write_complete_ts < db_mtime_observed_post` (the witness boundary).

### E2E (existing target `tests/e2e_concurrency.rs`)
- [ ] **EXISTING `e2e_read_command_witness_refresh_waits_for_write_lock` passes**
- [ ] **EXISTING `e2e_parallel_read_only_commands_serialize_without_busy_on_drop` passes**
- [ ] **NEW** `e2e_50_iter_witness_refresh_no_flake` — runs the same scenario 50× in one test invocation; passes only if all 50 pass; emits a tracing summary at end with `pass_count`, `fail_count`, `total_ms`, `seeds_used`.
- [ ] **NEW** `e2e_concurrency_with_seed_env_var_is_deterministic` — runs twice with same seed, asserts identical observation sequences.

### Shell harness (new: `tests/e2e_scripts/concurrency_witness_logged.sh`)
- [ ] Drives N concurrent `br list` + 1 `br update` against a shared workspace, captures stderr from each, parses for any `WARN`/`ERROR` lines, asserts the final `br show <updated_id>` returns the post-update state and only the post-update state.
- [ ] Loops 50 iterations and reports per-iteration pass/fail.
- [ ] Emits a structured event log to `/tmp/concurrency_witness_<ts>.jsonl` with `{ts, pid, command, exit, observed_state, iteration}`.
- [ ] Exits 0 only if all 50 pass.

### Cross-platform smoke (optional but documented)
- [ ] If access to mmini (macOS arm64) and wlap (Windows x86_64) build hosts: run the 50-iter shell harness on each, document deltas in `docs/CONCURRENCY_NOTES.md` (new file or section).

## Logging requirements

- All `.write.lock` acquisitions must emit `tracing::debug!` with `holder_pid`, `wait_ms`, `attempt`, `lock_path` fields.
- Witness refresh events must emit `tracing::info!` with `db_mtime_before`, `db_mtime_after`, `wait_for_lock_ms`, `seed` (if BCV_CONCURRENCY_SEED set).
- E2E tests must `RUST_LOG=info` and capture stderr to `/tmp/mjmk_concurrency_<ts>.log` on failure.
- On panic, emit a structured JSON dump of the observation log so post-mortem doesn't require re-running.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo test --release --test e2e_concurrency --no-fail-fast` exits 0
- [ ] 50× flake test passes (added unit + new e2e) — 50/50 pass under both BCV_CONCURRENCY_SEED=42 and BCV_CONCURRENCY_SEED=1337
- [ ] `cargo test --release --test proptest_concurrency` exits 0
- [ ] New shell harness exits 0 and emits structured event log
- [ ] BCV_CONCURRENCY_SEED env var documented in `docs/TESTING_GUIDELINES.md` (created in linked sibling)
- [ ] (If cross-platform access available) Cross-platform smoke documented in `docs/CONCURRENCY_NOTES.md`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [ ] No new `unsafe_code`

## Verification command

```bash
cd /data/projects/beads_rust
RUST_LOG=info BCV_CONCURRENCY_SEED=42 RCH_DISABLED=1 cargo test --release --no-fail-fast \
  --test e2e_concurrency --test proptest_concurrency \
  -- --nocapture 2>&1 | tee /tmp/mjmk-verify.log
echo "exit: $?"
bash tests/e2e_scripts/concurrency_witness_logged.sh
```

## Source

beads_compliance_audit pass `2026-05-09T01-00-44Z`, Class E real failure. Parent: `beads_rust-c827`. Grandparent EPIC: `beads_rust-ebzi`. **Blocks: yyxo** (sync-safety must ship first). Possibly related: `beads_rust-kw8p`.
close_reason: Root cause: test fixture only corrupted jsonl_size; the staleness probe falls back to hash comparison, and hash still matched → probe returned 'not newer' → search never blocked. Fix: extend fixture to also corrupt jsonl_content_hash. e2e_concurrency 175/175 pass; 50/50 flake-check zero flake; concurrency_witness_logged.sh 50-iter harness PASS. Clippy + fmt clean. Loom/shuttle + cross-platform smoke deferred (additive observability).

title: Standardize MCP display limit constants across tools.rs and resources.rs
description:

description:
EPIC: Comprehensive audit found numerous hardcoded magic numbers, duplicated inline constants, and deferred-implementation markers across the codebase. This epic tracks all remediation work.

title: search Command Implementation (FTS5)
description:
## Overview
Implement the `br search` command for full-text search across issues using SQLite FTS5. This enables fast, relevance-ranked searches across issue titles, descriptions, and comments.

## CLI Interface
```
br search <query> [OPTIONS]

Arguments:
  <query>                   Search query (supports FTS5 syntax)

Options:
  -t, --type <TYPE>         Filter by issue type
  -s, --status <STATUS>     Filter by status
  -p, --priority <PRIORITY> Filter by priority (0-4)
  -l, --label <LABEL>       Filter by label (repeatable)
  --limit <N>               Maximum results (default: 50)
  --offset <N>              Skip first N results
  --json                    Output as JSON
  --robot                   Machine-readable output
```

## Technical Requirements

### FTS5 Virtual Table Schema
```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS issues_fts USING fts5(
    id, title, description,
    tokenize = "porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2"
);

-- Keep FTS in sync with triggers
CREATE TRIGGER issues_fts_insert AFTER INSERT ON issues BEGIN
    INSERT INTO issues_fts(id, title, description)
    VALUES (NEW.id, NEW.title, NEW.description);
END;

CREATE TRIGGER issues_fts_delete AFTER DELETE ON issues BEGIN
    DELETE FROM issues_fts WHERE id = OLD.id;
END;

CREATE TRIGGER issues_fts_update AFTER UPDATE ON issues BEGIN
    DELETE FROM issues_fts WHERE id = OLD.id;
    INSERT INTO issues_fts(id, title, description)
    VALUES (NEW.id, NEW.title, NEW.description);
END;
```

### Search Implementation
```rust
impl SqliteStorage {
    pub fn search_issues(&self, query: &str, filter: &SearchFilter) -> Result<Vec<IssueWithScore>> {
        let sql = r#"
            SELECT i.*, bm25(issues_fts) as score
            FROM issues i
            JOIN issues_fts f ON i.id = f.id
            WHERE issues_fts MATCH ?1
              AND (?2 IS NULL OR i.status = ?2)
              AND (?3 IS NULL OR i.issue_type = ?3)
            ORDER BY score
            LIMIT ?4 OFFSET ?5
        "#;
        // Execute and map results
    }
    
    pub fn rebuild_fts_index(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
        self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM issues_fts", [])?;
        self.conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO issues_fts SELECT id, title, description FROM issues", []
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

### FTS5 Query Syntax Support
- Simple terms: `authentication bug`
- Phrase search: `"login failed"`
- Prefix search: `auth*`
- Boolean: `auth AND NOT password`
- Column filters: `title:authentication`
- NEAR: `NEAR(login password, 5)`

## Output Formats

### Human-readable
```
Search results for "authentication bug":
1. [bd-abc12] [BUG] P0 Authentication fails silently
   ...the authentication system throws no error when...
   Score: 0.95
Found 2 matches (50ms)
```

### JSON
```json
{
  "query": "authentication bug",
  "results": [{
    "id": "bd-abc12", "title": "...", "score": 0.95,
    "snippet": "...the authentication system..."
  }],
  "total": 2, "elapsed_ms": 50
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] FTS5 virtual table created in schema migration
- [ ] Triggers maintain FTS index on CRUD
- [ ] BM25 relevance ranking
- [ ] Filters combine with FTS (type, status, priority, labels)
- [ ] Pagination (limit, offset)
- [ ] Snippet generation with highlighting
- [ ] Human-readable and JSON output
- [ ] rebuild_fts_index() for repair
- [ ] Graceful handling of invalid FTS5 syntax

## Unit Tests
- Basic term search
- Phrase search ("exact phrase")
- Prefix search (term*)
- Boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT)
- Column filters (title:term)
- BM25 ranking verification
- Filter combinations
- Empty results
- Invalid syntax error handling
- FTS sync after CRUD

## Dependencies
- Database Schema and Migrations
- SQLite Storage Layer Core
- Model Types (IssueWithScore)

## Rationale
Full-text search is essential for issue discovery in large projects. FTS5 provides O(log n) relevance-ranked search with minimal code.

title: CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)
description:
# CI/CD Pipeline

## Purpose
Implement GitHub Actions workflows for continuous integration and release automation. This ensures code quality, catches regressions, and automates the release process.

## Files to Create

### .github/workflows/ci.yml
```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

jobs:
  check:
    name: Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@stable
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-01-01
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - name: Cache cargo registry
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

      - name: Check (all targets)
        run: cargo check --all-targets

  test:
    name: Test Suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: check
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@stable
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-01-01

      - name: Cache cargo registry
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: cargo test --lib -- --nocapture
        env:
          RUST_LOG: beads_rust=debug

      - name: Run integration tests
        run: cargo test --test integration -- --nocapture
        env:
          RUST_LOG: beads_rust=debug

      - name: Run snapshot tests
        run: cargo test --test snapshots

      - name: Run doc tests
        run: cargo test --doc

  coverage:
    name: Code Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@stable
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-01-01
          components: llvm-tools-preview

      - name: Install cargo-llvm-cov
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov

      - name: Generate coverage report
        run: cargo llvm-cov --all-features --workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
        with:
          files: lcov.info
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  bench:
    name: Benchmarks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@stable
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-01-01

      - name: Run benchmarks
        run: cargo bench --bench storage_perf -- --noplot

      - name: Store benchmark result
        uses: benchmark-action/github-action-benchmark@v1
        with:
          tool: 'cargo'
          output-file-path: target/criterion/*/new/estimates.json
          fail-on-alert: true
          alert-threshold: '150%'
          comment-on-alert: true

  build:
    name: Build (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: test
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - os: macos-latest
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
          - os: macos-latest
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
          - os: windows-latest
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@stable
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-01-01
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Build release binary
        run: cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: br-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: |
            target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/br
            target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/br.exe

  conformance:
    name: Conformance Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@stable
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-01-01

      - name: Install bd (Go beads)
        run: |
          # Install from release or build from source
          go install github.com/example/beads/cmd/bd@latest

      - name: Run conformance tests
        run: cargo test conformance -- --nocapture
        env:
          BD_PATH: $(which bd)
          RUST_LOG: debug
```

### .github/workflows/release.yml
```yaml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  create-release:
    name: Create Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      upload_url: ${{ steps.create_release.outputs.upload_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Create Release
        id: create_release
        uses: actions/create-release@v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          release_name: Release ${{ github.ref_name }}
          draft: true
          prerelease: ${{ contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}

  build-release:
    name: Build Release (${{ matrix.target }})
    needs: create-release
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            archive: tar.gz
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            archive: tar.gz
          - os: macos-latest
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            archive: tar.gz
          - os: macos-latest
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            archive: tar.gz
          - os: windows-latest
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
            archive: zip
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-action@stable
        with:
          toolchain: nightly-2025-01-01
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Install musl tools
        if: matrix.target == 'x86_64-unknown-linux-musl'
        run: sudo apt-get install -y musl-tools

      - name: Build release binary
        run: cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Create archive (Unix)
        if: matrix.archive == 'tar.gz'
        run: |
          cd target/${{ matrix.target }}/release
          tar -czvf br-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ matrix.target }}.tar.gz br
          mv br-*.tar.gz ../../../

      - name: Create archive (Windows)
        if: matrix.archive == 'zip'
        run: |
          cd target/${{ matrix.target }}/release
          7z a br-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ matrix.target }}.zip br.exe
          mv br-*.zip ../../../

      - name: Upload Release Asset
        uses: actions/upload-release-asset@v1
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          upload_url: ${{ needs.create-release.outputs.upload_url }}
          asset_path: br-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ matrix.target }}.${{ matrix.archive }}
          asset_name: br-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ matrix.target }}.${{ matrix.archive }}
          asset_content_type: application/octet-stream
```

### .github/workflows/audit.yml
```yaml
name: Security Audit

on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/Cargo.toml'
      - '**/Cargo.lock'
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * *'  # Daily at midnight

jobs:
  audit:
    name: Security Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run cargo audit
        uses: rustsec/audit-check@v2
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

## Local Development Scripts

### scripts/ci-local.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run CI checks locally before pushing

set -e

echo "=== Formatting ==="
cargo fmt --all -- --check

echo "=== Clippy ==="
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

echo "=== Tests ==="
cargo test --all

echo "=== Doc tests ==="
cargo test --doc

echo "=== Build release ==="
cargo build --release

echo "=== All checks passed! ==="
```

### scripts/bench-compare.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Compare benchmarks between branches

BASELINE_BRANCH=${1:-main}
CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)

echo "Comparing $CURRENT_BRANCH against $BASELINE_BRANCH"

# Run baseline
git stash
git checkout $BASELINE_BRANCH
cargo bench --bench storage_perf -- --save-baseline baseline

# Run current
git checkout $CURRENT_BRANCH
git stash pop
cargo bench --bench storage_perf -- --baseline baseline

# Compare
critcmp baseline current
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] .github/workflows/ci.yml with check, test, build jobs
- [ ] .github/workflows/release.yml for automated releases
- [ ] .github/workflows/audit.yml for security scanning
- [ ] Cross-platform builds (Linux, macOS, Windows)
- [ ] Code coverage reporting
- [ ] Benchmark comparison on main branch
- [ ] Conformance tests in CI (optional, if bd available)
- [ ] Local CI script for pre-push validation
- [ ] Release artifacts uploaded to GitHub Releases
- [ ] Cache optimization for faster builds

## Dependencies
- Requires test infrastructure complete
- Requires benchmark infrastructure
- Requires all tests passing locally

## Rationale
CI/CD automation ensures consistent quality and catches issues before they reach main. Automated releases reduce manual work and ensure reproducible builds across platforms. The benchmark comparison catches performance regressions before they ship.

title: JSONL discovery + metadata.json handling
description:
# JSONL Discovery + metadata.json Handling

## Purpose
Implement safe JSONL file selection and metadata.json startup config, matching bd rules.

## JSONL Selection Rules
1. Prefer `issues.jsonl` if present.
2. Else fall back to `beads.jsonl` (legacy).
3. Never treat `deletions.jsonl`, `interactions.jsonl`, or merge artifacts
   (`beads.base.jsonl`, `beads.left.jsonl`, `beads.right.jsonl`) as the main JSONL.
4. If none exists, default to `issues.jsonl` for writing.

## Path Inputs
- `BEADS_JSONL` env var (highest priority for JSONL path).
- `metadata.json` field `jsonl_export` (relative to `.beads/`).
- If DB path is overridden, derive JSONL path from DB directory.

## metadata.json
- Read before DB open to determine DB filename + JSONL filename.
- If missing, use defaults (`beads.db`, `issues.jsonl`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Discovery rules exclude merge artifacts and legacy deletion logs.
- `metadata.json` overrides respected.
- Safe default when no JSONL exists.

## Tests
- Fixtures with multiple JSONL candidates.
- metadata.json override path test.
close_reason: JSONL discovery fully implemented in config/mod.rs: BEADS_JSONL env var, DB override, metadata.json override, file discovery (issues.jsonl > beads.jsonl), exclusion of merge artifacts. 15+ tests covering all cases.

title: [P2] Fuzz: no coverage for search_issues free-text query input
description: Gap: SqliteStorage::search_issues at src/storage/sqlite.rs:2413 accepts a free-form &str query from CLI args (br list --search <query>). This is an untrusted input surface with no fuzz coverage. While the query is used as a parameterized SQL bind value (not interpolated), the search logic includes string manipulation for FTS matching, LIKE pattern construction, and result filtering. Unusual inputs (NUL bytes, very long strings, Unicode edge cases, SQL-like syntax, empty strings) could trigger panics, logic errors, or unexpected query behavior. Related uncovered surfaces include add_comment (src/storage/sqlite.rs:5092, user-supplied text) and parse_date_reference (src/cli/commands/changelog.rs:336, user date strings). Target fuzz harness: new search_query fuzz target. Invariant to assert: (1) search_issues(&str) never panics on arbitrary input; (2) results are always a subset of stored issues (no phantom results); (3) error messages are non-empty on failure. Implementation: seed a SqliteStorage with known issues, then fuzz the search query string and verify results are valid issue IDs from the seeded set.
close_reason: Added search_issues libFuzzer target that feeds arbitrary byte strings through SqliteStorage::search_issues, validates returned issues with IssueValidator, checks results are seeded issues, and verified with cargo fuzz check plus a 2000-run smoke session via rch.

title: ID Resolution & Prefix Matching
description:
# ID Resolution & Prefix Matching

## Purpose
Implement classic partial ID resolution and prefix validation used by show/update/close/dep/etc.

## Partial ID Resolution
Order:
1. Exact ID match (`SearchIssues` by IDs).
2. Normalize: if missing prefix, prepend `issue_prefix-` and retry exact match.
3. Substring match on hash portion across all prefixes.
4. Ambiguity => error with candidate list.

## Prefix Validation
- Explicit IDs must match `issue_prefix` or `allowed_prefixes` unless `--force`.
- Trailing hyphen in prefix input is accepted; stored prefix has **no** trailing hyphen.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Matches bd resolution order and ambiguity handling.
- Hierarchical IDs (`bd-abc.1`) supported.

## Tests
- Exact, prefix, hash-only, substring matching.
- Ambiguous match error lists candidates.

(1) sync.rs:1270 — "For now, fail on conflicts. Future: interactive resolution or force flags." The sync merge currently hard-fails on any conflict. (2) history.rs:443 — "Let us shell out to diff -u for now as it is standard on linux/mac." The history diff command shells out to the system diff binary. The dep list command sorts dependencies by ID string instead of by priority. For triage workflows, priority-sorted deps would be more useful but requires an extra DB query per dependency.

title: Consolidate transaction and storage constants in sqlite.rs
description:
PARENT TASK 2 of 7: src/storage/sqlite.rs contains two identical function-local definitions of transaction retry parameters: MAX_RETRIES=5 and base_backoff_ms=10 at lines 218 and 615. title: Propagate MAX_TITLE_CHARS to all consumer sites across the codebase
description:
SUBTASK 1.6: After MAX_TITLE_CHARS is defined in validation/mod.rs, update every other location that hardcodes 500 for the title limit.

CONSUMER SITES (exhaustive list):

1. src/mcp/tools.rs:553 — CreateIssueTool validation: if title.is_empty() || title.chars().count() > 500
   Change to: use crate::validation::MAX_TITLE_CHARS; ... > MAX_TITLE_CHARS

2. src/mcp/tools.rs:1131 — UpdateIssueTool title validation: same pattern
   Change to: > MAX_TITLE_CHARS

3. src/storage/schema.rs:21 — SQL DDL: title TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length(title) <= 500)
   Change to: format!("title TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length(title) <= {MAX_TITLE_CHARS})")
   NOTE: This is in a static SQL string (SCHEMA_SQL). If it is a const &str, it cannot use format!(). In that case, add a comment referencing MAX_TITLE_CHARS and note the coupling. Alternatively, if the schema is built dynamically, use the const.

4. src/storage/schema.rs:747 — Migration SQL: "TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(length(title) <= 500)"
   Same approach as #3.

5. src/storage/sqlite.rs:10441 — Another SQL DDL occurrence
   Same approach as #3.

6. MCP tool description strings at tools.rs lines ~828, ~1070, ~1081, ~1314 — these mention "max 500 characters" in the tool schema descriptions that agents read. Update the description strings to reference the actual limit value.

IMPORTANT: For SQL DDL strings that are compile-time constants (const &str), you cannot use format!() at const time in stable Rust. The approach is: (a) if the string is built at runtime (in a function), use format!(), or (b) if it is a top-level const, add a comment "// Must match validation::MAX_TITLE_CHARS" and leave the literal, or (c) use the const_format crate. Evaluate which approach fits best given the existing code structure.

DEPENDS ON: Subtask 1.1 (defining the const).
close_reason: Propagated MAX_TITLE_CHARS to mcp/tools.rs (validation logic + coupling comments in schema descriptions), schema.rs (coupling comment), sqlite.rs (coupling comment). SQL DDL strings use comments since they cannot interpolate Rust consts.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: CRITICAL CONSIDERATION: SQL DDL strings in schema.rs and sqlite.rs may be compile-time const &str. Rust does not support format!() in const context. Options: (1) If the DDL is built in a function at runtime, use format!() with the const. (2) If it is a top-level const &str, add a comment // Must match validation::MAX_TITLE_CHARS = 500 and leave the literal. (3) Use the const_format crate for compile-time format strings. Option 2 is simplest and least invasive. The coupling comment ensures future changes are caught in review.

title: Fix blocked cache rebuild SQL parse error after issue writes

2. `./target/debug/br close beads_rust-586v --reason ... --json`

title: capabilities: advertise each fixer's --only/--skip filter id (fm-…) in the envelope
description: Found during the beads_rust-yx0b coverage audit.
