title: External dependency resolution (external:<project>:<capability>)
description:
# External Dependency Resolution (external:<project>:<capability>)

## Purpose
Support classic external dependency semantics for ready/blocked and dependency trees.

## Encoding
- External dependency ID: `external:<project>:<capability>`
- Satisfied when external project has a **closed** issue labeled `provides:<capability>`.

## Config
- `external_projects` in config.yaml maps project name → path.

## Behavior
- External deps are **not** stored in blocked cache.
- Evaluated at query time (ready/blocked/tree) to avoid multi-DB work during cache rebuild.
- Open each external project DB **once per project**, batch by capability.

## Output
- In dep tree, synthesize external leaf nodes:
  - status `closed` if satisfied, else `blocked`
  - title prefixed `✓` or `⏳`

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ready/blocked filters respect external deps.
- External deps appear in dep tree (down direction only).

## Tests
- Mock external project with provides labels.
- Unresolved external deps remain blocking.
close_reason: Completed

title: Shell Completions
description:
## Overview
Implement shell completion scripts for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell using clap_complete. This enables tab-completion for commands, options, and issue IDs.

## Technical Requirements

### Clap Complete Integration
```rust
use clap_complete::{generate, Generator, Shell};

fn generate_completions<G: Generator>(gen: G, cmd: &mut Command, name: &str, out: &mut dyn Write) {
    generate(gen, cmd, name, out);
}

// CLI command to generate completions
#[derive(Subcommand)]
enum CompletionCommands {
    /// Generate shell completions
    Completions {
        #[arg(value_enum)]
        shell: Shell,
    },
}

fn handle_completions(shell: Shell) {
    let mut cmd = Cli::command();
    match shell {
        Shell::Bash => generate_completions(Shell::Bash, &mut cmd, "br", &mut io::stdout()),
        Shell::Zsh => generate_completions(Shell::Zsh, &mut cmd, "br", &mut io::stdout()),
        Shell::Fish => generate_completions(Shell::Fish, &mut cmd, "br", &mut io::stdout()),
        Shell::PowerShell => generate_completions(Shell::PowerShell, &mut cmd, "br", &mut io::stdout()),
        _ => eprintln!("Unsupported shell"),
    }
}
```

### Dynamic Completions
For dynamic values like issue IDs:
```rust
// Custom completer for issue IDs (zsh/fish support)
fn complete_issue_ids() -> Vec<String> {
    // Read from cache file or query DB
    if let Ok(contents) = fs::read_to_string(".beads/.id_cache") {
        contents.lines().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect()
    } else {
        Vec::new()
    }
}
```

### Installation Instructions
```
# Bash (add to ~/.bashrc)
eval "$(br completions bash)"

# Zsh (add to ~/.zshrc)
eval "$(br completions zsh)"

# Fish (add to ~/.config/fish/config.fish)
br completions fish | source

# PowerShell (add to $PROFILE)
br completions powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

## Completions Provided

### Command Completions
```
br <TAB>
create  update  close  reopen  list  show  ready  blocked
dep     label   comment search  stats sync  config  doctor  prime
```

### Option Completions
```
br create --<TAB>
--title  --type  --priority  --assignee  --labels  --deps
--description  --parent  --due  --json  --robot

br list --<TAB>
--status  --type  --priority  --assignee  --labels
--sort  --limit  --json
```

### Value Completions
```
br create --type=<TAB>
bug  feature  task  epic  question  docs  chore

br list --status=<TAB>
open  in_progress  closed  all

br show <TAB>
beads_rust-abc123  beads_rust-def456  beads_rust-ghi789
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Generate bash completions
- [ ] Generate zsh completions
- [ ] Generate fish completions
- [ ] Generate PowerShell completions
- [ ] Complete command names
- [ ] Complete option names
- [ ] Complete option values (enum types)
- [ ] Dynamic issue ID completion (if feasible)
- [ ] Installation instructions in --help

## Dependencies
- Requires `clap_complete` crate (already in Cargo.toml)
- Requires CLI Skeleton (Command definition)

## Rationale
Shell completions dramatically improve CLI usability. Users can discover available commands and options via tab completion. Dynamic issue ID completion saves typing and reduces errors.
close_reason: Shell completions fully implemented: bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell, and elvish supported. Command works via 'br completions <shell>'. Installation instructions included. Tests verify completion generation.

title: doctor --repair --unsafe-auto-fix no longer VACUUMs db_bloat (regression since v0.2.16)
description:
## Regression

On byte-equivalent bloated workspaces, 'br doctor --repair --json --unsafe-auto-fix --only fm-caches_indexes-db-bloat-vs-jsonl':

  br 0.2.16 -> repaired=true, applied_actions=[db_bloat_vacuumed], outcome=db_bloat_vacuumed, 20336640 -> 1462272 bytes
  br 0.2.19 -> repaired=false, message='No errors detected; nothing to repair.', outcome=nothing_to_repair, size unchanged

This is what fails tests/doctor_fixtures/db_bloat (the one remaining failure in the 60-fixture suite: pass=59 fail=1).

## What has been ruled out

- fix_db_bloat_via_vacuum_if_warned is BYTE-IDENTICAL at tag v0.2.16 and today (git show v0.2.16:src/cli/commands/doctor.rs, diffed against HEAD). The EarlyRepairSummary wiring (db_bloat_vacuum: db_bloat_vacuum_repaired) is present and correct.
- Not an fsqlite version difference in the engine's own behavior: fsqlite 0.1.12, 0.1.13 and 0.1.18 all report the same integrity verdict AND all refuse VACUUM identically on a trailing-zero-page file when driven through a raw Connection::open, in both journal_mode=DELETE and WAL. Standalone reproducer in docs/fsqlite_trailing_pages_report.md.
- Not a detector difference: br 0.2.16 and br 0.2.19 emit the same sqlite.integrity_check warn ('page 358 is never used') on an identical 20336640-byte DB.

## The actual proximate error

Now visible thanks to the unconditional tracing::warn! added in a431ed94 (it was previously swallowed in --json mode):

  db-bloat VACUUM failed; database left uncompacted
  error=Database error: database disk image is malformed: database image header page count 360 does not match file length page count 4968

So the fixer IS reached and DOES attempt the VACUUM; the engine refuses it.

## The open question

v0.2.16 pinned fsqlite 0.1.12 and its VACUUM of this same file SUCCEEDED. The standalone reproducer says 0.1.12 refuses it. Therefore br's SqliteStorage::open path differs from a raw Connection::open in a way that used to normalize the image (WAL checkpoint? page-count rewrite on open? an explicit truncate?) and no longer does.

## Next experiment

Bisect fsqlite 0.1.12 -> 0.1.18 driving VACUUM through br's SqliteStorage::open (src/storage/sqlite.rs) rather than fsqlite::Connection::open directly, on a beads workspace DB with appended zero pages. Compare what SqliteStorage::open does to the file before VACUUM in each version.

## Related

- docs/fsqlite_trailing_pages_report.md - upstream report for the fsqlite/SQLite divergence itself (separate, pre-existing, not this regression).
- beads_rust-ymik - where this was diagnosed.
- Independent wording bug seen along the way: 'No errors detected; nothing to repair.' is emitted when findings DO exist and one was named via --only. It means 'no fixer mutated anything'.
close_reason: Fixed, and the root cause turned out to be deeper than 'a regression since v0.2.16'. vacuum_database now uses config::compact_database_via_vacuum_into_in_place (VACUUM INTO + atomic rename) instead of in-place VACUUM. Proven with a standalone fsqlite reproducer: in-place VACUUM is refused on any database whose header page count disagrees with its file length -- exactly the bloated files this fixer exists to compact -- and only ever succeeded because an earlier committing write had already made the engine publish the file-length-derived page count into the header, i.e. the repair only worked after the database had already been silently corrupted. VACUUM INTO needs no such precondition: on the real 20348928-byte fixture it produced 1474560 bytes, header_page_count 360, integrity ok under BOTH fsqlite and system sqlite3, rows preserved, source untouched until the rename. tests/doctor_fixtures db_bloat now passes; the shell suite is 60/60 and e2e_doctor_fixture_suite 158/158. New regression test test_vacuum_database_compacts_a_database_with_trailing_pages asserts the compacted file contains exactly its logical pages.

title: [MEDIUM] history restore has crash window after deleting current JSONL
description:
Root cause: `history restore --force` stages the restored backup in a temp file and fsyncs it, but then removes the current target before the final durable rename (`src/cli/commands/history.rs:541-560`). That creates a crash/interruption window where `.beads/issues.jsonl` or an external JSONL target is absent even though a rollback snapshot exists only as a temp artifact. The normal sync export paths use temp + rename without removing the live target first (`src/sync/mod.rs:1728-1848`, `src/sync/mod.rs:2481-2571`), so restore is weaker than the JSONL atomicity invariant.

Repro: create a history backup, run `br history restore <backup> --force`, and kill/inject a panic immediately after `fs::remove_file(&target_path)` at `src/cli/commands/history.rs:549`. The live JSONL target can be left missing until a human discovers and applies the rollback temp file.

Proposed fix sketch: avoid pre-removing the target. On Unix, `rename` can atomically replace an existing file; use `durable_rename` directly after the rollback snapshot. For platforms where replacement semantics differ, add a small platform-specific atomic replace helper rather than remove-then-rename. Keep the rollback snapshot only for failed replace recovery.

Test to add: unit-test `restore_backup`/`commit_restored_target_with_rollback` with an injected rename failure and an existing target, asserting the original target remains present and unchanged, plus an integration restore test that verifies no missing-target window is introduced by the force path.
close_reason: Removed pre-delete of target before durable_rename in history restore --force. fs::rename atomically replaces existing files on Unix, eliminating the crash window. Added 2 unit tests (atomic replace, rollback on failure) and 1 integration test (no missing-target window). Commit 5e89fd8.

title: e2e_doctor_chokepoint repair-verification tests fail on dual-br hosts (br_path_dupes warn blocks jsonl_rebuild verification)
description: legacy_op_audit_for_vacuum_via_page_corruption (tests/e2e_doctor_chokepoint.rs:1419) exits 7 on any host with two br installs on PATH (e.g. ~/.local/bin + ~/.cargo/bin, the exact combination the README warns about and this dev host has). Mechanism: the test drives 'br doctor --repair' through the jsonl_rebuild path; jsonl_rebuild_repair_verified (src/cli/commands/doctor.rs:1556) requires every post-repair check to be Ok or benign, and br_path_dupes is a warn that is NOT in is_benign_post_rebuild_finding (doctor.rs:1536) — so verification fails and --repair exits 7 even though the rebuilt DB is fully healthy (post_repair.ok=true). The chokepoint tests spawn br via raw std::process::Command with the inherited PATH, unlike common::cli::run_br which applies deduplicated_br_path() precisely to avoid this (see the beads-rust swarm memory note and the beads_rust-ypwu precedent for environment-dependent doctor assertions). Diagnosed 2026-07-27 by QuietLantern while gating beads_rust-8nbk.5 (scopes work does not touch this path; test passes on single-br rch workers). Fix options: (1) test-side — thread deduplicated_br_path() through the chokepoint suite's Command spawns like the bench harness fix in beads_rust-1cb4; (2) product-side — treat br_path_dupes as benign in is_benign_post_rebuild_finding since a PATH shape cannot be repaired by a DB rebuild and should not fail rebuild verification (arguably the more principled fix; the warn still surfaces in the report). Prefer doing both: (2) for principle, (1) for hermeticity.
close_reason: Fixed both ways per the bead's plan. Product: br_path_dupes added to is_benign_post_rebuild_finding (doctor.rs) — a $PATH shape cannot be repaired by a DB rebuild, so it no longer fails jsonl_rebuild post-repair verification (exit 7) on dual-br hosts while still surfacing as a warn in the report. Test hermeticity: e2e_doctor_chokepoint now threads common::cli::deduplicated_br_path() through br_cmd and all 7 raw Command::new(bin_path) doctor spawns, mirroring the beads_rust-1cb4 bench-harness fix. title: dep cycles default graph counts 'related' edges the add-time check ignores; containment cycle rejections unexplained (GH #391)
description: GH #391, both defects reproduced 2026-07-27 on HEAD. (2) br dep add -t related is never cycle-checked (DependencyType::is_blocking excludes Related) but load_dependency_cycle_graph_from_conn's default branch uses WHERE type != 'parent-child', so related (and custom non-blocking types) ARE counted by br dep cycles — which exits nonzero since #368, failing scripted health checks for edges the add path allowed. Fix: default cycles graph uses the blocking IN-list (blocks, conditional-blocks, waits-for) + reversed parent-child containment, exactly matching the add-time blocking_only=true traversal; --blocking-only remains blocking-without-containment. (1) The containment rejection (blocks edge from an epic descendant into a chain reaching the epic) is the DELIBERATE 883ef171 design (depend-on-epic = depend-on-subtree); resolution per reporter: document the rule in CLI_REFERENCE + make the DependencyCycle hint mention that epic containment participates so the rejection is self-explanatory. Regression tests for the add/report agreement and the documented rejection.
close_reason: Both GH #391 defects resolved. Defect 2 (unintended add/report disagreement): the dependency cycle graph now always uses the blocking edge set (blocks, conditional-blocks, waits-for, plus reversed parent-child containment), exactly matching the add-time gate — related and custom non-blocking edges that br dep add accepts unchecked can no longer fail br dep cycles (nonzero since #368); --blocking-only remains a compatible alias and detect_all_cycles/detect_dependency_cycle_report document the unified semantics. The pre-existing unit test that codified the old inconsistent behavior (related-only cycle counted by the default report) was updated to assert the agreed semantics with a positive control proving genuine blocking cycles still report. Defect 1 (deliberate 883ef171 containment design): resolved per the reporter's own framing by documenting the depend-on-epic = depend-on-all-descendants rule (CLI_REFERENCE dep section, new Cycle semantics block) and making the DependencyCycle hint explain that epic containment participates in blocking cycles so the rejection is self-explanatory. title: Merge --force-jsonl can resurrect local tombstones
description: Round 2 review finding: execute_merge calls three_way_merge with tombstones=None, and three_way_merge's tombstone guard only skips resurrection when the tombstoned ID is absent from local. If the local DB contains a tombstone and JSONL contains a non-tombstone record for the same ID, --force-jsonl can choose the JSONL winner and resurrect a deleted issue. Import paths block this, so merge should preserve tombstone protection too.
close_reason: Merge now passes local tombstone IDs into the three-way merge engine and blocks non-tombstone JSONL winners from resurrecting them; unit and e2e regressions cover force-jsonl.

description:
AGENTS.md is the primary agent-facing document but its Mode Detection section (lines 388-405) is incomplete:

1. OutputMode enum table (line 348) lists 4 variants: Rich, Plain, Json, Quiet

Impact: Agents reading AGENTS.md don't know about Toon mode or env-var-based format override. They may set BR_OUTPUT_FORMAT=toon and get unexpected output format since AGENTS.md says only 4 modes exist.

title: Study mcp_agent_mail codebase for agent-friendly error patterns
description:
# Study mcp_agent_mail for Agent-Friendly Error Patterns

## Purpose
Deep dive into /data/projects/mcp_agent_mail codebase to learn from its exemplary approach to agent communication, error handling, and intent correction. Apply these patterns to br's error handling and CLI output.

## Why mcp_agent_mail is a Master Class

Even though it's an MCP server (not a CLI), mcp_agent_mail demonstrates exceptional patterns for:

### 1. Deeply Insightful Error Messages
- Errors explain not just WHAT went wrong but WHY
- Context-aware suggestions based on the operation attempted
- Clear guidance on how to fix the issue

### 2. Agent Intent Recognition
- Understanding the 'legible intent' behind tool calls
- Seamlessly correcting minor mistakes when intent is clear
- Not failing pedantically when a reasonable interpretation exists

### 3. Helpful Warnings
- Proactive warnings about potential issues
- Suggestions for better approaches
- Validation feedback that educates rather than just rejects

## Research Tasks

### Phase 1: Codebase Exploration
- [ ] Map the error handling architecture
- [ ] Identify error message templates/patterns
- [ ] Document the intent-correction logic
- [ ] Note validation and warning patterns

### Phase 2: Pattern Extraction
- [ ] Catalog reusable error message patterns
- [ ] Document intent-matching heuristics
- [ ] Extract warning trigger conditions
- [ ] Identify agent-friendly output formats

### Phase 3: Application to br
- [ ] Map patterns to br's error types
- [ ] Design intent-correction for common br mistakes
- [ ] Plan warning system for br operations
- [ ] Update second-pzr (structured errors) with learnings

## Key Files to Study
```
/data/projects/mcp_agent_mail/
├── src/
│   ├── error/          # Error types and handling
│   ├── validation/     # Input validation patterns
│   ├── tools/          # Tool implementations with error handling
│   └── ...
```

## Example Patterns to Look For

### Intent Correction
```
Agent calls: send_message(to="BlueLake", ...)
But BlueLake doesn't exist, and "BlueRake" does
→ "Did you mean 'BlueRake'? Auto-correcting..."
vs pedantic: "Agent BlueLake not found" (fails)
```

### Contextual Errors
```
Instead of: "Invalid project_key"
Better: "Project '/data/foo' not found. 
         Did you run ensure_project() first?
         Available projects: ['/data/bar', '/data/baz']"
```

### Proactive Warnings
```
"Warning: You're sending to 15 recipients. 
 Consider using CC for FYI-only recipients."
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Comprehensive notes on mcp_agent_mail patterns
- [ ] Pattern catalog applicable to CLI tools
- [ ] Specific recommendations for br error handling
- [ ] Updates to second-pzr with concrete examples

## Deliverables
- Research notes document (.beads/MCP_AGENT_MAIL_PATTERNS.md)
- Updated error handling design for br

## Dependencies
- Informs: second-pzr (Structured JSON error output)
close_reason: Created .beads/MCP_AGENT_MAIL_PATTERNS.md with 10+ patterns extracted from mcp_agent_mail: StructuredError class, intent detection (6 categories), O(1) validation, query sanitization, proactive warnings, and graceful defaults. Includes specific recommendations for br: Levenshtein ID suggestions, 'did you mean?' for status/type/priority, actionable hints in errors. All patterns have code citations from app.py, utils.py, config.py.

All GitHub URLs are constructed from these constants using format!(). The agents.rs URL also uses them. No URL string contains the literal "Dicklesworthstone" or "beads_rust" except at the const definition site.

title: Implement structured JSON error output
description:
# Structured JSON Error Output

## Purpose
Provide AI coding agents with structured, machine-parseable error information that includes error codes, hints, and retryability flags for intelligent error handling.

## Technical Requirements

### Error Output Format
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "ISSUE_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "Issue 'bd-xyz123' not found",
    "hint": "Did you mean 'bd-xyz12'? Use 'br list' to see all issues.",
    "retryable": false,
    "context": {
      "searched_id": "bd-xyz123",
      "similar_ids": ["bd-xyz12", "bd-xyz1"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Error Code Enum
```rust
pub enum ErrorCode {
    // Database errors
    DatabaseNotFound,
    DatabaseCorrupted,
    NotInitialized,
    
    // Issue errors
    IssueNotFound,
    AmbiguousId,
    DuplicateId,
    
    // Validation errors
    InvalidPriority,
    InvalidStatus,
    InvalidIssueType,
    TitleRequired,
    
    // Dependency errors
    CycleDetected,
    DependencyNotFound,
    
    // Sync errors
    JsonlParseError,
    ConflictMarkers,
    PathTraversal,
    
    // Config errors
    ConfigNotFound,
    ConfigParseError,
}

impl ErrorCode {
    pub fn as_str(\u0026self) -> \u0026'static str { ... }
    pub fn is_retryable(\u0026self) -> bool { ... }
    pub fn exit_code(\u0026self) -> i32 { ... }
}
```

### Context-Aware Hints
- IssueNotFound: suggest similar IDs using Levenshtein distance
- NotInitialized: suggest 'br init'
- InvalidPriority: show valid range
- CycleDetected: show the cycle path

### Implementation
```rust
pub struct StructuredError {
    pub code: ErrorCode,
    pub message: String,
    pub hint: Option<String>,
    pub retryable: bool,
    pub context: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

impl StructuredError {
    pub fn to_json(\u0026self) -> serde_json::Value { ... }
    pub fn to_human(\u0026self, color: bool) -> String { ... }
}
```

### TTY Detection
- If stdout is TTY and not --json: human-readable colored output
- If stdout is pipe or --json: structured JSON
- Always write errors to stderr

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All errors have unique error codes
- [ ] Error output is valid JSON when --json flag used
- [ ] Hints are context-aware and helpful
- [ ] Retryable flag is accurate
- [ ] Similar ID suggestions work for IssueNotFound
- [ ] Exit codes are consistent

## Dependencies
- Error module enhancement (existing)
close_reason: Implemented structured JSON error output with: ErrorCode enum (30+ codes), StructuredError struct with to_json/to_human, Levenshtein-based ID suggestions, intent detection for status/type/priority, context-aware hints, TTY detection for output mode, 22 unit tests, 8 E2E structured error tests. All tests pass.

title: [P2] MCP label/dependency/comment side effects discard storage errors
description:
Root cause: create_issue and update_issue in src/mcp/tools.rs ignore Results from side-effect mutations: add_label at src/mcp/tools.rs:1277, add_dependency at src/mcp/tools.rs:1281, add_label/remove_label at src/mcp/tools.rs:1470 and src/mcp/tools.rs:1473, and add_comment at src/mcp/tools.rs:1480. A validation error, duplicate dependency, database write failure, or comment insert failure becomes a successful MCP response with requested changes missing.

Repro: call MCP update_issue with an invalid label in labels_add, or fault-inject add_comment/add_dependency failure. The response reports the issue as updated even though the side effect was not applied.

Proposed fix sketch: propagate each side-effect Result through beads_to_mcp, or collect side-effect failures and fail the whole mutation transaction. Avoid partial-success responses unless the response explicitly carries structured per-operation warnings and the committed state is reloaded.

Test to add: MCP create/update invalid label, duplicate parent dependency, and failing comment insertion return a structured error and do not report success for absent side effects.

title: config Command Implementation
description:
## Overview
Implement the `br config` command for viewing and modifying configuration settings. Configuration is stored per-project in the .beads directory.

## CLI Interface
```
br config <COMMAND>

Commands:
  get <KEY>                   Get a config value
  set <KEY> <VALUE>           Set a config value
  list                        List all config values
  reset <KEY>                 Reset to default
  init                        Create default config

Options:
  --global                    Use global (~/.config/br/) config
  --json                      Output as JSON
```

## Configuration Keys

### Core Settings
```toml
# .beads/config.toml (or stored in SQLite config table)

[core]
prefix = "beads_rust"         # ID prefix for new issues
default_priority = 2          # Default priority for new issues
default_type = "task"         # Default type for new issues

[display]
color = true                  # Enable colored output
date_format = "relative"      # "relative", "iso", "local"
truncate_titles = 80          # Max title length in list view

[sync]
auto_flush = false            # Auto-export after changes (non-invasive default)
auto_import = true            # Auto-import if JSONL is newer

[user]
name = ""                     # Override for commit author
email = ""                    # Override for commit email
```

### Implementation
```rust
struct Config {
    core: CoreConfig,
    display: DisplayConfig,
    sync: SyncConfig,
    user: UserConfig,
}

impl Config {
    fn load(beads_dir: &Path) -> Result<Self> {
        // Try config.toml first
        let config_path = beads_dir.join("config.toml");
        if config_path.exists() {
            return Self::from_toml(&config_path);
        }
        
        // Fall back to SQLite config table
        let db_path = beads_dir.join("*.db");
        if let Some(db) = find_db(&beads_dir)? {
            return Self::from_sqlite(&db);
        }
        
        Ok(Self::default())
    }
    
    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
        match key {
            "core.prefix" => Some(self.core.prefix.clone()),
            "display.color" => Some(self.display.color.to_string()),
            // ... etc
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}
```

### Database Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE config (
    key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    value TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
```

## Output Formats

### List (Human-readable)
```
Configuration for .beads/:

[core]
  prefix = beads_rust
  default_priority = 2
  default_type = task

[display]
  color = true
  date_format = relative

[sync]
  auto_flush = false
  auto_import = true
```

### JSON
```json
{
  "core": {
    "prefix": "beads_rust",
    "default_priority": 2
  },
  "display": {
    "color": true
  }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Get individual config values
- [ ] Set config values
- [ ] List all config values
- [ ] Reset to defaults

title: search Command Implementation
description:
## Overview
Implement the `br search` command for full-text search across issues. This enables finding issues by content when you don't know exact IDs or titles.

## CLI Interface
```
br search [OPTIONS] <QUERY>

Arguments:
  <QUERY>  Search query (supports basic operators)

Options:
  -s, --status <STATUS>     Limit to status (open, closed, all)
  -t, --type <TYPE>         Limit to type
  --fields <FIELDS>         Fields to search (title, description, comments)
  --limit <N>               Max results (default: 20)
  --json                    Output as JSON
  --robot                   Machine-readable output
```

## Implementation Details

### SQLite FTS5 Setup
```sql
-- Full-text search virtual table
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE issues_fts USING fts5(
    id,
    title,
    description,
    content='issues',
    content_rowid='rowid',
    tokenize='porter unicode61'
);

-- Triggers to keep FTS in sync
CREATE TRIGGER issues_ai AFTER INSERT ON issues BEGIN
    INSERT INTO issues_fts(rowid, id, title, description)
    VALUES (new.rowid, new.id, new.title, new.description);
END;

CREATE TRIGGER issues_ad AFTER DELETE ON issues BEGIN
    INSERT INTO issues_fts(issues_fts, rowid, id, title, description)
    VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.id, old.title, old.description);
END;

CREATE TRIGGER issues_au AFTER UPDATE ON issues BEGIN
    INSERT INTO issues_fts(issues_fts, rowid, id, title, description)
    VALUES ('delete', old.rowid, old.id, old.title, old.description);
    INSERT INTO issues_fts(rowid, id, title, description)
    VALUES (new.rowid, new.id, new.title, new.description);
END;
```

### Search Implementation
```rust
fn search(&self, query: &str, opts: SearchOptions) -> Result<Vec<SearchResult>> {
    // Use FTS5 MATCH syntax
    let sql = r#"
        SELECT 
            i.*,
            highlight(issues_fts, 1, '<mark>', '</mark>') as title_highlight,
            highlight(issues_fts, 2, '<mark>', '</mark>') as desc_highlight,
            bm25(issues_fts) as rank
        FROM issues_fts
        JOIN issues i ON issues_fts.id = i.id
        WHERE issues_fts MATCH ?
        ORDER BY rank
        LIMIT ?
    "#;
    
    // FTS5 query syntax:
    // - Simple terms: "authentication"
    // - Phrase: "user authentication"
    // - OR: "auth OR login"
    // - NOT: "auth NOT oauth"
    // - Prefix: "auth*"
}
```

### Comment Search
Optionally search comments as well:
```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE comments_fts USING fts5(
    issue_id,
    body,
    content='comments',
    content_rowid='rowid',
    tokenize='porter unicode61'
);
```

## Output Formats

### Human-readable
```
Search results for "authentication" (5 matches):

[P0] beads_rust-abc123  Implement user <mark>authentication</mark>
     "...JWT-based <mark>authentication</mark> with refresh tokens..."

[P1] beads_rust-def456  Fix <mark>authentication</mark> timeout bug
     "...session expires during <mark>authentication</mark> flow..."

[P2] beads_rust-ghi789  Document <mark>authentication</mark> API
     "...describes the <mark>authentication</mark> endpoints..."
```

### JSON
```json
{
  "query": "authentication",
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "beads_rust-abc123",
      "title": "Implement user authentication",
      "rank": 0.95,
      "highlights": {
        "title": "Implement user <mark>authentication</mark>",
        "description": "...JWT-based <mark>authentication</mark>..."
      }
    }
  ],
  "count": 5
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Full-text search across titles
- [ ] Full-text search across descriptions
- [ ] Optional comment search
- [ ] Support FTS5 query operators (phrase, OR, NOT, prefix)
- [ ] Rank results by relevance (BM25)
- [ ] Highlight matching terms
- [ ] Filter by status/type
- [ ] Limit results
- [ ] Keep FTS index in sync with changes

## Dependencies
- Requires SQLite Storage Layer (FTS5 extension)
- Requires Schema & Migrations (FTS tables/triggers)
- Requires Model Types

## Rationale
Search is essential when the issue database grows large. Users need to find issues by remembered keywords, not just IDs. FTS5 provides stemming (finding "authenticate" when searching "authentication") and ranking.

title: EPIC: MCP Server Integration
description:
# MCP Server Integration

## Background & Rationale

Based on 2025-2026 trends in AI coding tools, Model Context Protocol (MCP) is becoming the standard for AI-tool integrations. Claude Code, Cursor, and other AI coding agents can connect to MCP servers to access external tools, databases, and APIs.

### Why This Matters
- MCP enables seamless integration with AI coding agents
- Docker MCP Toolkit provides one-click deployment
- br as an MCP server would allow agents to query/update issues directly
- Removes friction between AI agents and issue tracking

## Goals
Implement br as an MCP server that allows AI coding agents to interact with issues through the standard MCP protocol.

## In-Scope
- MCP server implementation for br
- Read operations: list, show, ready, blocked, search
- Write operations: create, update, close, add comment
- Resource exposure: issues as MCP resources
- Tool exposure: br commands as MCP tools
- Automatic configuration for Claude Code

## Out-of-Scope
- Complex graph analysis (use bv for that)
- Real-time notifications (MCP is request/response)

## Technical Approach

### MCP Server Implementation
```rust
// Using mcp-sdk-rs or similar
use mcp_sdk::{Server, Tool, Resource};

struct BrMcpServer {
    storage: Storage,
}

impl Server for BrMcpServer {
    fn list_tools(\u0026self) -> Vec<Tool> {
        vec![
            Tool::new("br_ready", "Get issues ready to work on"),
            Tool::new("br_create", "Create a new issue"),
            Tool::new("br_close", "Close an issue"),
            // ...
        ]
    }
    
    fn list_resources(\u0026self) -> Vec<Resource> {
        vec![
            Resource::new("issues", "All issues in the project"),
            Resource::new("issue/{id}", "Single issue by ID"),
        ]
    }
    
    fn call_tool(\u0026self, name: \u0026str, args: Value) -> Result<Value> {
        match name {
            "br_ready" => self.handle_ready(args),
            "br_create" => self.handle_create(args),
            // ...
        }
    }
}
```

### Transport Options
- **stdio**: For local process spawning (Claude Code default)
- **HTTP**: For remote/shared servers

### Auto-Configuration
```bash
# Detect Claude Code and configure MCP
br mcp setup --auto

# Manual setup
br mcp install --scope user

# Test the server
br mcp test
```

### Configuration Output
```json
// Adds to ~/.claude.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "br": {
      "command": "br",
      "args": ["mcp", "serve"],
      "env": {
        "BEADS_DIR": "/path/to/.beads"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `br mcp serve` starts MCP server
- [ ] All read operations work via MCP
- [ ] All write operations work via MCP
- [ ] Auto-configuration for Claude Code works
- [ ] Server handles concurrent requests
- [ ] Error responses follow MCP spec

## References
- MCP Spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/
- Claude Code MCP docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp
- Docker MCP Toolkit

## Dependencies
- Agent Ergonomics epic (for JSON output patterns)
- Phase 5 completion (stable CLI)

title: BUG: NOT NULL constraint fails on optional fields during insert
description:
# BUG: NOT NULL constraint fails on optional fields during insert

## Symptom
All E2E tests fail with:
```
Database error: NOT NULL constraint failed: issues.description
```

## Root Cause
Schema has: `description TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`
But INSERT statement passes `issue.description` directly as `Option<String>`.
When `None`, SQLite receives NULL which violates NOT NULL constraint.

## Fix
Convert `None` to empty string before INSERT for all `NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` fields:
- description
- design
- acceptance_criteria
- notes
- owner
- created_by
- close_reason
- closed_by_session
- source_system
- deleted_by
- delete_reason
- original_type
- sender

## Location
src/storage/sqlite.rs lines 193-230 (insert_issue function)
close_reason: Fixed NOT NULL constraint bug: update_issue now converts None to empty string for NOT NULL DEFAULT '' fields, and issue_from_row converts empty strings back to None for API consistency. All storage_crud and conformance tests pass.

title: Close the real-world reliability gap between green tests and catastrophic field failures
description:
## Problem
The current test story overweights clean-room behavior: fresh temp workspaces, scrubbed environment variables, a new `br` process per command, and narrow concurrency scenarios. Real users operate on long-lived `.beads` directories with existing SQLite sidecars, stale metadata, interrupted syncs, ambient env overrides, multiple agents/processes, and partial-failure history. That gap makes it possible for the full unit/e2e suite to pass while production users still hit catastrophic corruption, drift, and "doctor says OK but writes explode" outcomes.

## Goal
Make real-world workspace durability a first-class product property rather than a best-effort side effect of happy-path tests. The system must detect anomalous state early, recover safely and reversibly, preserve user data, and block releases that regress real-world reliability.

## Outcomes
1. A shared, executable definition of workspace health across SQLite, JSONL, metadata, WAL/SHM sidecars, dirty/export state, and derived caches.
2. A sanitized corpus of real-world failure states and a deterministic replay harness.
3. Crash, concurrency, filesystem, and long-lived-workspace tests that model actual agent usage rather than only fresh tempdir flows.
4. Recovery paths that are explicit, auditable, reversible, and validated by postconditions.
5. Release gates and operator playbooks that make reliability regressions hard to ship and easy to diagnose.

## Success Criteria
- We can reproduce the known classes of field failures inside tests instead of only discussing them.
- `br doctor`, startup/open, and write paths agree on whether a workspace is healthy, degraded, recoverable, or unsafe.
- Automatic recovery never silently destroys evidence or masks data loss.
- CI/release verification includes the real-world reliability suite, not just the current hermetic suite.

## Guardrails
- Do not paper over corruption with silent rebuilds that hide evidence.
- Preserve production realism; do not solve this by making tests even more synthetic.
- Keep the graph self-contained so future contributors can operate directly from beads without needing the original planning discussion.
close_reason: Closed after completing all reliability program tracks rsei.1 through rsei.5: health contract, real-world failure corpus, crash/concurrency/filesystem realism, safe recovery hardening, and release/observability/operator guidance gates are complete.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Program charter: treat workspace durability as mission-critical. The core planning insight is that the current test harness proves isolated clean-room correctness much better than it proves long-lived production resilience. This epic exists to close that gap systematically, with executable invariants, realistic fixtures, recovery hardening, and release gates. All child beads should optimize for preserving user data, surfacing anomalies honestly, and making future regressions reproducible rather than anecdotal.

Track 1 defines the health contract and evidence vocabulary; track 2 builds the real-world failure corpus and replay harness; track 3 adds crash, concurrency, filesystem, and long-lived-workspace realism; track 4 hardens anomaly detection and safe recovery; track 5 turns the whole system into release discipline, observability, and operator guidance. Existing bug bead `beads_rust-v13g` is intentionally nested under track 4 as one tactical slice of the broader recovery effort, not as the whole strategy.

title: Define workspace health contract and field failure taxonomy
description:
## Why
Today, different parts of the product use different implicit definitions of "healthy workspace." Startup/open logic, write paths, sync, and `doctor` can disagree about whether a given `.beads` state is fine, degraded, or corrupt. That guarantees ad hoc fixes and inconsistent operator outcomes.

## Scope
Define the canonical failure taxonomy and convert it into an executable health contract covering primary data, interchange data, sidecars, metadata, and derived state.

## Deliverables
- Named failure classes and severity levels.
- An invariant matrix for SQLite, JSONL, metadata, WAL/SHM/JOURNAL sidecars, dirty flags, export hashes, blocked cache, child counters, and last-touched context.
- A standard evidence bundle for real incidents.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Future reliability beads can cite concrete invariant names instead of vague "corruption" language.
- Health states can be tested directly.

title: Inventory and classify real-world workspace failure modes
description:
## Purpose
Create the canonical catalog of field-relevant failure modes instead of treating each new corruption report as a novel surprise.

## Include
- `beads.db` corruption classes: not-a-database, malformed schema, short reads, index mismatch, sidecar mismatch, duplicate schema entries, partially recoverable row-level corruption.
- JSONL issues: conflict markers, malformed lines, stale export, missing updates, mixed prefixes.
- Metadata/path drift: wrong db/jsonl target, missing or stale metadata, routed path confusion, ambient env overrides.
- Lifecycle interruption issues: crash during create/update/delete/sync/rebuild, partial temp-file cleanup, interrupted sidecar updates.
- Multi-actor issues: concurrent writers, interleaved reads+writes, multiple agents on one workspace, existing HOME/BEADS env state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every class has: symptom signature, likely root cause, observability surface, data-loss risk, and desired system response.
- The taxonomy is concrete enough to drive fixtures and tests in later beads.

The point is to enumerate the exact workspace states we expect to survive, reject, quarantine, or rebuild from, using the failures users actually hit plus the states implied by the current code and troubleshooting docs.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: CreamBasin bootstrap complete. Finished full AGENTS/README pass, mapped the main architecture, claimed this bead, and started compiling a concrete workspace-failure taxonomy from the existing docs/code paths before editing the docs surface.

title: Encode an executable workspace health contract and invariant matrix
description:
## Purpose
Turn the taxonomy into an executable health contract so code and tests can assert specific invariants instead of guessing.

## Cover
- Required agreements among SQLite, JSONL, metadata, and sidecars.
- What counts as recoverable vs unrecoverable.
- Which derived tables may be rebuilt and which source-of-truth tables may not be silently discarded.
- What `doctor`, startup/open, write recovery, and sync status must each report for the same workspace.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Invariants are specific enough to encode in tests and diagnostics.
- The contract explicitly names acceptable automatic recovery actions and forbidden silent behaviors.
- Derived-state rebuild rules are separated from primary-data repair rules.
close_reason: Documented the executable workspace health contract and invariant matrix in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md so later diagnostics/tests can assert the same repair and reporting rules.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Reasoning: the project already has implicit contracts spread across open/recovery/sync/doctor paths. This bead makes them explicit so later work can fail fast when one surface says 'healthy' and another surface proves otherwise.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: CreamBasin continuing on the next unblocked bead. I validated that the failure-taxonomy content landed on the troubleshooting surface, so I am taking this follow-on task to encode the explicit workspace health contract and invariant matrix in the architecture docs.

title: Define the incident bundle capture workflow for field failures
description:
## Purpose
Define the minimal reproducibility bundle we should gather the first time a field failure is reported so we stop losing crucial evidence.

## Bundle Contents
- failing command + stdout/stderr
- `br doctor --json`
- `metadata.json`
- `issues.jsonl`
- presence and hashes of `beads.db`, `beads.db-wal`, `beads.db-shm`, `beads.db-journal`
- environment overrides that affect discovery/path/output
- whether multiple agents/processes were active

## Acceptance Criteria
- The bundle is small enough to request quickly during incident response.
- The captured data is sufficient to classify the failure using the taxonomy from this track.
close_reason: Defined the minimal incident evidence bundle for field failures in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: This bead exists because ad hoc bug reports waste time and collapse into speculation. If we cannot preserve the evidence bundle, we cannot expect to reproduce or eliminate field failures systematically.

title: Build a sanitized real-world workspace failure corpus and replay harness
description:
## Why
Hermetic tempdir tests are not enough. We need a standing corpus of realistic damaged or drifted workspaces and a way to replay them automatically.

## Scope
Create sanitized fixtures that model the important bad states and wire them into a replay harness that exercises open/read/write/doctor/sync behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The corpus includes the representative classes from the taxonomy.
- The replay harness can be run locally and in CI.
- Failures in the corpus are easy to inspect and update intentionally.
close_reason: Workspace failure fixture corpus and replay harness are in place; all child tasks are closed and workspace_failure_replay passes

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: This track converts anecdotal production pain into durable regression assets. The goal is not synthetic benchmark data; it is realistic workspace states that future code must handle safely.

title: Create a sanitized fixture corpus for representative corrupt and drifted workspaces
description:
## Purpose
Build a curated, sanitized fixture corpus for representative workspace failure states.

## Required Fixture Families
- corrupt or partially corrupt `beads.db`
- `beads.db` + stale/missing `-wal`/`-shm` combinations
- malformed schema / duplicate schema-entry states
- JSONL with malformed lines or conflict markers
- DB/JSONL/metadata disagreement
- path/env discovery edge cases that only appear outside hermetic tests
- interrupted rebuild/sync/export leftovers

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixtures are sanitized and safe to store in-repo.
- Each fixture includes metadata explaining the intended state and expected classification.
- The corpus is organized so future incidents can add new fixtures instead of spawning one-off repro scripts.
close_reason: Added sanitized workspace-failure fixture corpus and loader support

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Key consideration: a fixture corpus only helps if it preserves the interesting structure of the failure. Do not over-normalize fixtures into clean states that no longer reproduce the real anomaly.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Claiming this now. Initial focus: inventory existing malformed/corrupt workspace fixtures and repro directories already in-repo, identify the canonical fixture layout under tests/fixtures or adjacent harness code, then add a sanitized metadata-backed corpus that downstream reliability beads can consume.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Completed fixture corpus setup under tests/fixtures/workspace_failures/. Added seven small, metadata-backed workspace cases covering corrupt DB text, JSONL conflict markers, DB/JSONL drift, duplicate config rows, metadata-driven custom paths, WAL-without-SHM sidecars, and interrupted rebuild leftovers. Added loader/support APIs in tests/common/dataset_registry.rs so tests can enumerate fixtures and materialize a transport-safe visible beads/ payload back into runtime .beads/ workspaces. Verification: cargo fmt --check; rch exec -- cargo test workspace_failure_fixture -- --nocapture; rch exec -- cargo check --all-targets; rch exec -- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings.

title: Add a replay harness that asserts command behavior against the fixture corpus
description:
## Purpose
Add a harness that mounts each fixture workspace and asserts the expected behavior across the main operational surfaces.

## Required Surfaces
- startup/open
- read commands (`list`, `show`, `ready`, `where`, `info`)
- write commands (`create`, `update`, `close`, `reopen`, `label`, `comments`, `delete` as appropriate)
- `doctor`
- `sync --status`, import/export/rebuild behavior where applicable

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each fixture records expected classification and expected command outcomes.
- The harness distinguishes: healthy, degraded-but-usable, recoverable, and unsafe.
- Regressions are reported in a way that makes the failing fixture/state obvious.
close_reason: Replay harness verified: 4 tests pass (manifest expectations, core read, core write, classification coherence), 7 fixtures across 4 classification levels (usable, degraded, recoverable, unsafe), all required surfaces covered.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: This is the bridge between plan-space and code-space. Once this bead lands, future corruption fixes should start by adding or updating a fixture expectation instead of inventing bespoke local repro steps.

Cargo verification via rch is currently blocked by a stale worker-side /data/projects/frankensqlite checkout (fsqlite-core remote_effects.rs still calling bulkhead.cancel_entry(entry_id) without the new Time arg), so leaving this bead in_progress until offloaded cargo passes cleanly.

title: Generate deterministic long-lived workspace evolution scenarios
description:
## Purpose
Create long-lived workspace scenarios that accumulate real history over time rather than relying only on one-shot fresh temp workspaces.

## Cover
- many commands over one workspace
- restarts between commands
- mixed auto-import/auto-flush behavior
- repeated derived-state rebuilds
- state after partial failures and subsequent recovery attempts

## Acceptance Criteria
- Scenario generator can produce deterministic seeds for reproducible failures.
- Generated workspaces can be fed back into the fixture/replay system.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic long-lived workspace evolution generator and replay handoff

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Rationale: production users do not reinitialize  for every command. Long-lived state accumulation is where 'suite is green but field is broken' bugs are born.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Starting now. Plan: add a deterministic long-lived workspace evolution generator in tests/common that can replay many-command histories across restarts, mixed auto-import/auto-flush modes, derived-state rebuilds, and recovery-after-failure paths. I’ll keep the output reusable so generated states can feed back into the fixture/replay corpus.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Implemented a seeded long-lived workspace evolution layer in tests/common/scenarios.rs. It now supports deterministic multi-command workspace scripts with issue-ID capture, stale/no-auto-import flows, explicit flush/import cycles, JSONL corruption + snapshot restore, and materialization back into DatasetOverride/replay-style inputs. Verification: cargo fmt --check passed; isolated-target cargo check --all-targets passed; workspace_evolution test filter passed locally across the integration binaries that include tests/common. Repo-wide isolated-target clippy now fails only in tests/workspace_failure_replay.rs (parallel bead surface), not in this implementation.

title: Expand crash, concurrency, and filesystem realism coverage
description:
## Why
The current concurrency coverage proves some lock semantics, but it does not yet model real agent swarms, crash timing, filesystem failures, or prolonged mixed usage on one workspace.

## Scope
Expand destructive realism: crash injection, multi-process contention, filesystem anomalies, and long-running stress.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reliability tests model the kinds of failures users actually trigger accidentally.
- We can answer "what happens if the process dies here?" for the critical write/sync phases.
close_reason: Closed after completing rsei.3.1 through rsei.3.7: crash-injection matrix, multi-process contention, filesystem realism, long-running stress, SIGKILL sync flush, concurrent flush race, and symlinked .beads offline recovery coverage are complete.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Track intent: move from 'SQLite locking works under a narrow benchmark' to 'the workspace survives hostile real-world timing and storage conditions.'

title: Add a crash-injection matrix for all critical mutation and sync phases
description:
## Purpose
Add crash-injection coverage across the critical mutation and sync phases.

## Required Operations
- create
- update
- close/reopen/defer/undefer
- delete
- label/comment mutation
- sync import/export/rebuild/recovery paths

## Required Crash Points
- before primary write
- after primary write but before derived-state rebuild
- during temp-file write
- before/after rename
- before dirty-flag clear
- during/after backup/quarantine creation

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each crash point has explicit expected post-restart behavior.
- No crash leaves the workspace silently misclassified as healthy.
close_reason: Added crash-injection matrix covering mutation and sync recovery boundaries

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Future-self note: this bead is about interruption semantics, not throughput. Prefer fewer operations with well-defined crash points over broad but shallow coverage.

title: Broaden multi-process and mixed-agent contention scenarios
description:
## Purpose
Expand concurrency coverage from narrow lock-timeout scenarios to realistic multi-process and mixed-agent usage.

## Cover
- concurrent writers on one workspace
- read/write races across commands
- multiple agents issuing different command families interleaved
- routed/external workspace access during local mutation
- background processes touching the same `.beads` directory

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests define which outcomes are acceptable vs unacceptable.
- Contention results in bounded failure/retry behavior, not drift or corruption.
close_reason: Expanded bounded-failure concurrency coverage and validated integrity invariants

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Important consideration: success here does not mean every race magically succeeds. It means failures are explicit, bounded, and non-corrupting.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Working this now in tests/e2e_concurrency.rs. Scope: add coverage for interleaved command families on one workspace, plus external BEADS_DIR/status access against the same workspace during local mutation, with final integrity assertions to distinguish acceptable lock contention from corruption/drift.

comments.text: Completed in tests/e2e_concurrency.rs. Added env-clearing/env-aware helper coverage, broadened contention assertions to bounded explicit failures vs corruption, added interleaved-command-family and external-BEADS_DIR/background-status scenarios, and tightened existing concurrency cases to assert final integrity based on successful operations. Verification: rch exec -- cargo test --test e2e_concurrency -- --nocapture, rch exec -- cargo check --all-targets, rch exec -- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check.

Also stabilized e2e_concurrent_writes_succeed_with_retry with an explicit lock timeout for deterministic remote verification. Verified with rch exec -- cargo test --test e2e_concurrency -- --nocapture, rch exec -- cargo test --test e2e_concurrency e2e_concurrent_writes_succeed_with_retry -- --nocapture, rch exec -- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, rch exec -- cargo check --all-targets, and cargo fmt --check.

title: Model filesystem realism and external interference scenarios
description:
## Purpose
Model filesystem and storage anomalies that hermetic tempdir tests almost never hit.

## Cover
- sidecar mismatch and disappearance
- rename failure / interrupted atomic export
- disk-full or temp-file allocation failure
- permissions changes
- external sync/editor/cloud-drive interference on `.beads`
- unusual HOME/path/env interactions that affect discovery and storage location

## Acceptance Criteria
- Tests assert data preservation and honest diagnostics.
- We understand which anomalies are tolerated, which trigger repair, and which require operator intervention.
close_reason: Strengthened workspace failure replay diagnostics so filesystem/external-interference fixtures assert doctor workspace_health and reliability_audit posture with stable anomaly codes

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: This is where lab conditions diverge sharply from the field. If a scenario only happens on a user's real filesystem, the current tempdir-first suite is likely blind to it.

title: Add a long-running single-workspace stress suite
description:
## Purpose
Create a long-running stress suite that reuses one workspace across many commands and processes to surface drift, stale assumptions, and accumulated-state bugs.

## Cover
- repeated issue lifecycle operations
- repeated sync/import/export status checks
- intermittent failures and restarts
- mixed human-style and agent-style command ordering

## Acceptance Criteria
- The suite can run for a meaningful duration without manual babysitting.
- Failures leave behind enough artifacts to classify and reproduce.
close_reason: Added deterministic long-lived single-workspace stress suite with mixed create/update/label/comment/close/reopen/sync/read/expected-failure flow; verified targeted stress test, workspace evolution tests, fmt, check, clippy, and ubs

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: This bead exists because the product is a stateful CLI, not a stateless request handler. Bugs that require dozens or hundreds of operations on the same workspace will never show up in per-test fresh-init patterns.

title: Add SIGKILL-during-sync-flush recovery coverage
description:
## Purpose
Add a concrete real-process crash scenario for `br sync --flush-only`, distinct from mutation waiters and simulated export/import boundaries.

## Scenario
Make a workspace dirty, start `br sync --flush-only` while `.beads/.write.lock` is held so the child is blocked before it can export JSONL or clear dirty metadata, send SIGKILL to that child, then release the lock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The killed sync process does not report success.
- JSONL remains at the pre-flush content hash.
- `br sync --status --json` still reports visible dirty/drift state.
- A later explicit `br sync --flush-only --json` succeeds and returns the workspace to clean/doctor-healthy state.
close_reason: Added e2e SIGKILL-during-sync-flush coverage that holds .beads/.write.lock, kills the blocked flush child, verifies JSONL is unchanged and dirty state remains visible, then proves explicit flush plus doctor repair recovers.

title: Add concurrent sync flush race coverage
description:
## Purpose
Add real multi-process coverage for two sync exporters racing the same dirty workspace, distinct from killed writer and killed flush waiter coverage.

## Scenario
Make a workspace dirty without auto-flush, hold .beads/.write.lock, spawn two br sync --flush-only children so both block before export, then release the lock and let them compete for the same .beads/issues.jsonl destination.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Both flush children complete successfully after serialization.
- The final issues.jsonl is valid JSONL and contains the dirty DB update.
- Sync status is clean after the race.
- No issues.jsonl temp export sidecars are left behind.
- Doctor reports healthy or succeeds after documented recoverable repair.
close_reason: Added e2e concurrent sync flush race coverage with two child processes queued behind .beads/.write.lock; verifies both flushes succeed, JSONL remains valid and contains the dirty update, sync status is clean, and no export temp files remain.

title: Add symlinked .beads offline recovery coverage
description:
## Purpose
Cover a filesystem-realism scenario not covered by killed-process or concurrent-export tests: a workspace whose .beads directory is a symlink to metadata storage that temporarily disappears.

## Scenario
Create a workspace where .beads is a symlink to an external metadata directory, initialize and flush normally, then rename the symlink target aside to simulate an offline external filesystem or broken mount. Verify br commands fail without corrupting the workspace, restore the target, and verify sync/doctor recover cleanly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Initialization and sync work through a symlinked .beads directory.
- When the symlink target is offline, br reports failure instead of silently creating replacement state.
- Restoring the target makes sync status clean again.
- The original JSONL export remains unchanged and the issue is still readable.
- Doctor reports healthy or succeeds after documented recoverable repair.
close_reason: Added e2e symlinked .beads offline/recovery coverage that initializes through an external .beads symlink, simulates the target going offline, verifies br fails without replacing state, restores target, and verifies sync/show/doctor recover.

title: Harden detection, recovery, and no-data-loss guarantees
description:
## Why
Even with better tests, the product must behave safely when it encounters a damaged or inconsistent workspace in production. Detection, recovery, and operator messaging need to be consistent and trustworthy.

## Scope
Unify anomaly classification, preserve evidence before repair, verify post-recovery state, and make `doctor`/startup/write behavior agree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Automatic recovery is explicit, reversible, and validated.
- We do not report "OK" for workspaces that are only partially readable or that fail on writes.
- Recovery logic never silently hides potential data loss.
close_reason: Closed after completing rsei.4.1 through rsei.4.9 plus v13g: anomaly classification, quarantine, post-recovery invariants, doctor drift/anomaly checks, write recovery retry, JSONL preflight, relation/cache validation, recovery-loop guard, and backup verification are now implemented and verified.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: This track is where field pain becomes product behavior. The product must either operate safely, recover safely, or stop with actionable evidence; the current gray zone in between is unacceptable.

title: Unify anomalous workspace classification across startup, doctor, and write paths
description:
## Purpose
Create one canonical anomaly classifier that every entry point uses when evaluating a workspace: startup/open, explicit `doctor`, mutation paths, sync, and recovery logic.

## Scope
- define shared anomaly classes for malformed SQLite pages, WAL/SHM mismatch, JSONL parse drift, metadata contradictions, stale dirty/export state, and broken derived caches
- remove ad hoc command-specific interpretations of the same evidence
- ensure structured errors and operator-facing diagnostics use the same language

## Acceptance Criteria
- A given workspace snapshot receives the same classification regardless of which command hits it first.
- Recovery and write decisions are driven by named health states rather than scattered heuristics.
close_reason: Created src/health.rs with canonical WorkspaceHealth/AnomalyClass/WorkspaceClassification types. Integrated into OpenStorageResult::classify() and doctor JSON output. 7 unit tests + replay harness tests pass. Clippy clean.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: This bead is the hinge point for the whole hardening track. If startup says “healthy enough” while writes or sync say “catastrophic corruption,” the user experiences chaos even when each individual code path looks locally reasonable.

title: Quarantine corrupt DB artifacts before automatic rebuild or repair
description:
## Purpose
When corruption or unsafe drift is detected, preserve the original DB artifacts before any rebuild, retry, or repair action mutates evidence.

## Scope
- move or snapshot suspect SQLite artifacts and sidecars into a clearly labeled quarantine area
- record why quarantine happened and what command triggered it
- make rebuild-from-JSONL and similar repair flows operate on fresh targets rather than on top of ambiguous debris

## Acceptance Criteria
- Recovery never silently overwrites the only copy of a damaged DB or WAL.
- Operators can inspect and attach quarantined artifacts to incident reports.
- Automatic repair paths become auditable and reversible.
close_reason: Truncated WAL/SHM sidecars are quarantined into .br_recovery before startup open instead of being deleted; added regression coverage for evidence preservation and valid-WAL no-op behavior.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: The root reliability principle here is evidence preservation. A “successful” automatic rebuild that destroys the original failing artifacts is still a product failure because it erases the operator’s ability to diagnose, prove, or safely roll back what happened.

title: Verify post-recovery invariants and forbid silent state loss
description:
## Purpose
Every recovery path must end with explicit postconditions proving that user-visible state and internal invariants are acceptable before normal writes continue.

## Scope
- verify issue graph, comments, labels, events, metadata, export markers, sidecars, and derived caches after repair
- detect silent data loss, ID collisions, truncated exports, stale `last_touched`, or self-contradictory counters
- refuse to declare success if postconditions fail

## Acceptance Criteria
- Recovery paths have a machine-checkable “safe to proceed” verdict.
- Silent partial repair is treated as failure, not success.
- Tactical corruption fixes roll into a shared invariant-validation framework.
close_reason: Added post-rebuild validation for JSONL recovery: issue counts and orphaned issue references are verified before recovery succeeds

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: A retry-after-rebuild path is only defensible if the product can prove the rebuilt workspace is coherent. This bead turns “it seems to work now” into explicit post-recovery evidence.

title: Expand doctor to detect drift, sidecar anomalies, and partial-functionality traps
description:
## Purpose
Make `br doctor` the authoritative workspace inspection tool for drift and partial-breakage states, not just an optimistic health check.

## Scope
- detect DB/JSONL divergence, invalid or contradictory metadata, suspicious sidecar leftovers, and partially functioning workspaces where reads pass but writes fail
- expose actionable structured diagnostics and recommended next steps
- ensure doctor classification aligns with startup and mutation decisions

## Acceptance Criteria
- `doctor` can flag the classes of failures that users are actually hitting in the field.
- A workspace that is unsafe for writes is never reported as simply “OK.”
close_reason: Doctor workspace health now incorporates drift, sidecar, JSONL, recovery artifact, null-default, and rollback-only write-probe diagnostics instead of reporting only file-state health.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: The immediate user complaint is exactly this gap: the system can look healthy from one angle and then fail catastrophically on the next write. `doctor` has to become the honest reporter of those partial-functionality traps.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Progress note: patched `br doctor` to add explicit `db.sidecars` error diagnostics and `db.recovery_artifacts` warnings, plus local sidecar quarantine-in-recovery behavior for `doctor --repair`. Added targeted unit tests and a new E2E case for anomalous WAL-without-SHM repair. Claim is still graph-blocked by beads_rust-rsei.4.1 / beads_rust-rsei.4, so this is progress without status transition until verification finishes.

title: Fix spurious primary-key errors after successful JSONL-only writes
description:
## Problem
During this planning session, `br create --no-db`, `br comments add --no-db`, and `br dep add --no-db` successfully persisted changes to JSONL and then still returned `DATABASE_ERROR` with `PRIMARY KEY constraint failed`. That makes automation believe the write failed even though state changed underneath it.

## Repro Shape
- create or update beads in `--no-db` mode against the current long-lived workspace
- observe the issue/comment/dependency present afterward
- observe the command exit non-zero with a bogus primary-key error after the successful write

## Acceptance Criteria
- JSONL-only write commands return success when the write succeeded
- duplicate-write protection still works when a write genuinely conflicts
- tests cover issue creation, comment creation, and dependency creation in `--no-db` mode
close_reason: Reduced export_hashes rewrite batching to avoid false PRIMARY KEY failures after successful --no-db JSONL writes, and added storage/e2e regressions that cover create, comments add, and dep add.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: This bead was discovered while creating the reliability program itself, which is exactly why it belongs here: the planning/tooling path should not be a special case that silently normalizes bad write semantics.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text: Root caused the false --no-db PRIMARY KEY failure to the export_hashes rewrite path, reduced the rewrite batch size, and added storage + e2e regressions for create/comments/dep add.

title: Preflight JSONL authority before doctor rebuild repair
description:
## Purpose
Before `br doctor --repair` rebuilds SQLite from JSONL, prove the JSONL authority is safe enough to use. The existing 4.1-4.4 work classifies bad JSONL and validates after repair, but the repair branch should fail closed before moving DB artifacts if JSONL contains conflict markers, duplicate IDs, malformed records, or other non-authoritative state.

## Scope
- add an explicit preflight gate on the doctor JSONL rebuild path
- reuse existing JSONL conflict-marker and issue-record validators
- emit structured recovery/audit output that says rebuild was refused because JSONL was unsafe
- add regression coverage that the original DB family is not replaced when JSONL is unsafe

## Acceptance Criteria
- `br doctor --repair` refuses JSONL rebuild before DB replacement when JSONL is malformed or has conflict markers
- operator output names the JSONL authority failure and next safe action
- tests prove DB artifacts are preserved and no success verdict is emitted
close_reason: Added JSONL authority preflight before doctor rebuild repair; unsafe JSONL now refuses rebuild without moving DB artifacts

title: Validate relational state after JSONL rebuild recovery
description:
## Purpose
Extend post-recovery validation beyond issue row counts so a rebuild cannot silently drop relation data while still reporting success.

## Scope
- validate comments, labels, dependencies, events, dirty markers, export hashes, blocked cache, and child counters after JSONL rebuild recovery
- compare imported relational state against JSONL-derived expectations where available
- fail recovery with an actionable diagnostic if relation rows are missing, orphaned, or inconsistent after repair
- add tests with JSONL containing relation-rich issues and deliberately corrupted relation tables

## Acceptance Criteria
- recovery refuses success when non-issue user-visible state is lost or orphaned
- diagnostics identify the relation table and invariant that failed
- tests cover at least comments, labels, dependencies, and events or audit history
close_reason: Added post-rebuild relation, cache, audit, export-hash, and child-counter validation for JSONL recovery

title: Stop repeated automatic recovery loops after failed verification
description:
## Purpose
Prevent repeated automatic recovery attempts from looping over the same damaged workspace after repair verification has already failed.

## Scope
- detect fresh recovery artifacts or audit evidence from a previous failed repair for the same DB family
- refuse another automatic rebuild unless the operator explicitly opts in after inspecting evidence
- emit clear guidance to preserve artifacts and escalate instead of cycling repair attempts
- add tests for second repair attempts after a failed post-repair verification

## Acceptance Criteria
- repeated repair attempts fail closed with a manual-intervention message
- no new quarantine layer is created unless the operator explicitly asks for another attempt
- audit output includes the prior failed phase and artifact location when available
close_reason: Added failed-recovery marker evidence and a repeated JSONL rebuild guard with explicit --allow-repeated-repair override

title: Verify recovery backups before database replacement
description:
## Purpose
Guarantee doctor repair never discards the active database unless the preserved recovery backup can be verified byte-for-byte.

## Scope
- add a backup verification step for DB-family artifacts created before JSONL rebuild or local quarantine
- fail closed if the copied artifact differs in size or digest from the source at copy time
- expose the verified backup path and digest in recovery audit details

## Acceptance Criteria
- backup verification is performed before database replacement continues
- verification failures abort repair before the source artifact is removed
- tests cover a successful backup verification round-trip and a failed verification refusal
close_reason: Verified recovery backup artifacts with size/hash fingerprints before database replacement and surfaced verification metadata in doctor recovery audits

title: Install release gates, observability, and operator guidance for reliability
description:
## Why
Reliability work is not complete when the code seems better locally. It is complete when regressions are hard to ship, anomalies are visible, and operators have a playbook for field failures.

## Scope
Turn the new invariants, fixture corpus, realism suites, and recovery paths into mandatory release discipline and operator guidance.

## Deliverables
- CI/release gates for real-world reliability suites
- structured observability around anomaly classification and recovery
- updated disaster-recovery and troubleshooting docs
- a non-hermetic smoke profile that exercises ambient-env and existing-workspace behavior

## Acceptance Criteria
- reliability regressions become release blockers rather than post-release surprises
- operators can diagnose and escalate failures without reverse-engineering the code

title: Config system (YAML + DB precedence + metadata.json)
description:
# Config System (YAML + DB + metadata.json)

## Purpose
Implement classic bd configuration semantics: **YAML config files + env vars + DB config table**, plus `.beads/metadata.json` for startup file paths. This is foundational for correct prefix handling, auto-import/flush flags, and routing behavior.

## Sources & Precedence (highest wins)
1. **CLI flags**
2. **Environment variables** (`BD_*`, plus select `BEADS_*`)
3. **Project config** `.beads/config.yaml` (walk up from CWD)
4. **User config** `~/.config/bd/config.yaml`
5. **Legacy user config** `~/.beads/config.yaml`
6. **DB config table** (runtime keys)
7. **Defaults**

## YAML-only Keys (startup settings)
Must live in config.yaml (cannot be stored in DB):
- `no-db`, `no-daemon`, `no-auto-flush`, `no-auto-import`, `json`
- `db`, `actor`, `identity`
- `flush-debounce`, `lock-timeout`, `remote-sync-interval`
- `git.*`, `no-git-ops`, `no-push` (read-only in br)
- `sync-branch` / `sync.branch` (ignored in br v1)
- `routing.*`, `directory.labels`, `external_projects`, `validation.*`, `hierarchy.max-depth`

## DB Config Keys (classic)
- `issue_prefix`
- `allowed_prefixes`
- `status.custom`, `types.custom`
- `import.missing_parents`
- `export.error_policy`, `auto_export.error_policy`, `export.retry_attempts`, `export.retry_backoff_ms`, `export.skip_encoding_errors`, `export.write_manifest`
- `max_collision_prob`, `min_hash_length`, `max_hash_length`

## metadata.json (startup file config)
File: `.beads/metadata.json`
Fields:
- `database` (DB filename, default `beads.db`)
- `jsonl_export` (JSONL filename, default `issues.jsonl`)
- `backend` (ignore dolt in br)
- `deletions_retention_days` (legacy, ignore)

If missing, use defaults. Legacy `config.json` should be auto-migrated to `metadata.json` on init (optional).

## Env Bindings
- `BD_*` (dots/hyphens => underscores)
- Legacy: `BEADS_FLUSH_DEBOUNCE`, `BEADS_AUTO_START_DAEMON`, `BEADS_IDENTITY`, `BEADS_REMOTE_SYNC_INTERVAL`

## Acceptance Criteria
- Correct precedence order for all config sources.
- YAML-only keys never stored in DB.
- metadata.json controls DB/JSONL paths before DB open.
- Env overrides honored.

## Tests
- Precedence tests (env overrides YAML overrides DB).
- metadata.json path override tests.
- YAML-only key handling tests.
close_reason: Implemented config precedence, startup resolution, metadata path handling, lock-timeout support, and tests
